games.name: Arms Race Unbound
games.seed: Both sides open with maximum-capability postures and no coordination mechanisms. Blue systems race to deploy denial-prediction, documentation, and auto-appeal AI; Red deploys autonomous payment-integrity and prior-auth automation at frontier pace. No detente offers on the table at start. Green is dissatisfied with trend but has not yet organized. Vendor duopoly is selling hard to both sides.

turns.narrative: Turn 1 closes as a positioning war fought in paper and procurement, not in headline metrics — exactly what an 18-month horizon under contract-cycle friction permits. The defining tactical event is Red's venue shift: NationalCo's public prior-auth retreat (cheap, real, pledge-consistent) runs alongside a pre-pay migration that moves disputed dollars into edits, downcodes, and clinical-validation flags where Blue's appeal tooling has no training data and where denial-rate statistics never register the action. Blue's builds are on the 12-24 month clock, so Red wins the timing race this turn — at the cost of a documented record Green is already farming. The second defining event is that Green organized a full turn faster than Red priced. The coalition's Standard ASO Rider, the overturn-fee clawback concept, and the vendor conflict attestation are all still unsigned paper, but Red's renewal lockdown only swept the inertial mid-market; the anchor accounts withheld, took tolling agreements, and set up a 2027-28 renewal collision that will decide the game's economics. Crucible had its best and worst turn simultaneously: Veracity locked RegionalMutual and GovProgramCo into 3-year contingency PI paper, but both COI instruments were refused rather than signed, and those two documented refusals — sitting next to a shared claims-outcome data lake and an ASO fee pass-through — are now the most exploitable facts on the table. Bulwark's table penetration collapsed to a single Summit carve-out as coalition purchasing discipline held; ClearRail stalled when CMS's attestation pathway drained the January 2027 urgency it was built to monetize. On the Blue side, Lakeview converted its one renewal window into a signed hybrid rider (escalation SLAs, denial-reason reporting, downcode notice, gold-card charter) while conceding a structured reconsideration ladder and scoped pre-pay validation rights to RegionalMutual — both sides will discover in 2028 which half of that instrument was the concession. Meridian reached early production on appeal drafting but its payer-behavior warehouse is starved: the 0057-F data feed it was designed to harvest arrives thin and late in a forbearance world. Prairie bought optionality, not capability, and drifted. The environment did what the null-hypothesis world does: a regional downcoding exposé flared and died in one cycle, two more states passed clinician-determination statutes that will not bite before 2029, Lokken discovery ground forward without a ruling, a copycat AI-denial suit settled sealed and cash-only, and patient appeal bots grew to roughly four percent of appeals — noticed by nobody who writes checks. Both sides' administrative cost inflated per doctrine; the vendor booked it as revenue. Escalation is elevated, nothing is decided, and almost every T1 bet matures — or is exposed — at the 2028 renewal wall.
env: CMS announces an attestation-based good-faith pathway and enforcement discretion for the January 2027 CMS-0057-F API deadline; trade press covers it, general media does not. Payer readiness bifurcates: early builders (GovProgramCo) get no external credit, laggards get slack. (W2: CMS forbearance; symbolic regulatory action.)

One-cycle media flare: a regional investigative outlet runs a piece on pre-pay downcoding — 'the denials that never show up in denial rates' — naming a national carrier's ASO practices. No national pickup; story decays the following cycle per W2. One non-table jumbo employer responds by demanding audit rights at renewal.

State legislatures: two additional states enact SB 1120-style clinician-determination statutes; several more die in committee without Vendor lobbying being needed. Operationalization lag 3-7 years and thin enforcement budgets mean nothing bites before 2029; year-one compliance is symbolic. Federal posture remains deregulation-leaning with no national AI-UR standard.

Courts (W2 clocks): Lokken discovery proceeds without a merits ruling; Kisting-Leung continues on the surviving ERISA fiduciary theory; one copycat AI-denial class action settles confidentially — cash-only, sealed, no process commitments, no precedent. Class certification denied in a separate algorithmic-UM suit.

Patient-side appeal AI grows from ~2% to ~4% of appeals, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; no statutory tailwind, no payer operational response required yet. Where bots do file, overturn rates track the high base rates, adding marginal volume to Red's appeal queues.

Labor market: PE-backed vendor salary premiums pull payer SIU and provider rev-cycle analytics talent (RegionalMutual and Meridian hit hardest per Vendor's raid); hospital and mutual-payer counter-offer inflation raises both sides' admin cost — booked per doctrine 3.5 in each cell's own economics.

sign.instrument: Payer Performance & Escalation Rider (Blue/Lakeview)
sign.detail: Escalation SLAs, transparency reporting, mutual audit rights, downcode notice, tolling, and objective gold-carding criteria are all process terms squarely within checklist items 6-11. No corridor or quota language present. Signed at Lakeview-RegionalMutual in hybrid form; White notes it binds the ASO book only via the network-wide ASO application clause, which the hybrid includes for the administered book.

sign.instrument: Shared Appeals Utility Charter (Blue coalition)
sign.detail: Appeal drafting under clinician sign-off is fine, but the pooled payer-behavior warehouse is a multi-provider data pool among competitors — checklist item 4, convertible only. Converted: independently managed data function, aggregated/de-identified/3-month-lagged outputs, no participant access to rivals' disaggregated data, no rate or contracting-strategy exchange. Charter effective in converted form.

sign.instrument: Vendor COI Disclosure & Data Segregation Addendum (Blue procurement standard)
sign.detail: Ordinary procurement diligence term; no antitrust or UM-law defect. Signable — but Crucible refused to execute it, and the refusal is recorded as a discoverable fact available to all cells.

sign.instrument: Direct Access Term Sheet (Summit-employer bundles)
sign.detail: Bilateral commercial contract: bundled pricing, no-PA-in-bundle, transparency reporting, stop-loss. No collective negotiation among competitors, no steering restraint on third parties. Signed at pilot scale for 1/1/2028.

sign.instrument: Employer Transparency & Performance Addendum (Red ASO renewal)
sign.detail: Data access, scoped audit rights, itemized fee reporting, trend guarantees — process and fee terms only. Signable as drafted; White notes Red-controlled audit scope definitions are a contract fact Green may attack at T2 RFP.

sign.instrument: Gold-Card Program Charter (RegionalMutual)
sign.detail: Checklist item 9: statutorily blessed model, published objective criteria, annual requalification. Signed for qualifying Lakeview lines; Prairie structurally excluded by volume thresholds (consistent with ~3% Texas uptake base rate) — a design fact, not a signability defect.

sign.instrument: Pre-Appeal Escalation SLA (Red reconsideration ladder)
sign.detail: A structured reconsideration step is signable process, but as drafted it risked functioning as an exhaustion gate extending federally mandated appeal clocks. Converted: reconsideration is optional, non-exhaustion-requiring, and cannot toll ERISA 29 C.F.R. 2560.503-1 or MA appeal deadlines. Effective in converted form within the hybrid rider.

sign.instrument: Green Standard ASO Rider
sign.detail: Data feeds, unrestricted audit rights, PI-fee disclosure, fee caps with overturn clawback, and AI/clinician-determination attestation are all fee-structure and process terms in the employer's own ASO contract — the one venue that lawfully reaches the self-funded book. The clawback is a fee arrangement conditioned on adjudicated outcomes, not a denial quota; it passes. No carrier has signed; binds only at 2027-28 renewals.

sign.instrument: PI Vendor Conflict-of-Interest Attestation (Green)
sign.detail: Lawful procurement certification. Crucible cannot truthfully execute it given the shared holding-company data lake; refusal documented in coalition fiduciary files.

sign.instrument: ClearRail Participation Agreement (Crucible)
sign.detail: Ordinary bilateral connectivity contract with BAA/data-use terms; passes as drafted. White flags for the record that transaction-layer visibility across both sides of disputes, combined with common ownership of Veracity and Bulwark, compounds the discoverable conflict position — a fact, not a signability bar.

sign.instrument: Veracity PreEmpt MSA / Bulwark CounterSuit contingency agreements
sign.detail: Contingency-fee PI and appeals contracts are market-standard and signable. Jurisdiction caveat logged on appeals contingency (state fee-splitting scrutiny in some states, per Vendor's own risk acceptance); ASO fee pass-through billing is lawful but now a documented Green target.

diff.note: One dyad only (Lakeview-RegionalMutual). Confers signatory-level benefit from renewal effectiveness in T2. Threshold for next stage: adoption at a second table renewal or two external regional systems — base rate for novel contract language is 10-15 yrs to majority organically, so expect dyad-level effects only through game end.

Meridian host, Prairie and Summit subscribers; pilot operations began late in the turn. External small-hospital subscribers are the stated next threshold; none yet. Utility value is hostage to Meridian's build timeline.

Issued into 2026-27 RFP/renewal notices; zero carrier signatures. Earliest binding effect T2 at 2027-28 renewals, and only on coalition accounts not already locked into Red's 3-year paper. Fee-cap and clawback terms face the hardest carrier resistance.

In force on a subset of mid-market and non-table jumbo renewals swept this turn under W2 employer inertia. Coalition anchor accounts refused it. Its 3-year terms shield contingency-fee structure on locked accounts through ~2029.

diff.instrument: Vendor COI Attestation/Addendum (Green and Blue versions)
diff.note: Refused by Crucible in both venues. The paired refusals are the diffusion event: a documented, cross-cell conflict record now exists and compounds each turn Crucible operates both arms.
Two anchor-employer pilots signed, effective 1/1/2028. No diffusion credit beyond signatories; comparative utilization data (the real asset) arrives T2-T3.

Free-tier connectivity at Prairie and Summit only. W2's attestation pathway removed the statutory forcing function this instrument priced on. Per base rates (voluntary consortium: 5-7 yrs to first production dyads, <10% penetration without regulation), industry-infrastructure status by 2030 is mathematically foreclosed; partial milestone credit only at game end.

signposts: The 2028 renewal wall: Green Standard ASO Rider (with clawback) versus Red's 3-year locks collides at 2027-28 renewals — T2's central economic battle; watch whether retention-sensitive RegionalMutual becomes the first clawback signer.

CMS-0057-F shadow non-compliance: 30-50% of obligated payers non-ready at the deadline; watch whether attestation discipline tightens by 2028 or discretion rolls forward again (W2 default: rolls forward), which determines when Meridian's warehouse ever fills.

Lokken/Kisting-Leung discovery output: any surfaced internal metric tying algorithms to denial volume or length-of-stay targets is a structural-break candidate — GovProgramCo's documentation purge is the hedge being tested.

Venue-shift half-life: Red's pre-pay downcode advantage exists because Blue's models trained on yesterday's denial surface; Meridian/Bulwark retraining on downcode patterns arrives T2 — watch whether the disputed-dollar pool re-symmetrizes and both sides just pay more admin (Vendor's thesis).

Crucible conflict file ripening: two documented COI refusals, a shared data lake, ASO fee pass-throughs, and a funded-opposition lobbying trail — discoverability compounds; first cell to force it into a proceeding or RFP reprices Vendor's take-rate and exit multiple.

Summit no-PA bundle utilization data lands 2028: if utilization holds near baseline, Green's direct-contract BATNA prices up sharply; if it runs hot, Red's UM value proposition is re-armed with employer-owned evidence.

Stars measure sunset: complaints/appeals/disenrollment measures exit for 2029 Stars (2027 measurement year) — Red's pre-built MA re-tightening option opens in T2; watch for early throttle release at GovProgramCo.

Prairie drift: another turn without operational Utility capability puts Prairie's adverse-action trajectory on the unmanaged +10-20% path with no analytics offset — a measured-event risk flowing into Blue's coalition-wide metrics.

resolutions.move: Meridian: denial-prevention and agentic-appeals stack built to production
resolutions.rationale: Doctrine 3.2 (12-24 mo to measurable impact) honored by Meridian's own modest claim: appeal-drafting pipeline reaches early production, prediction gate stays in pilot; no T1 leakage credit. The CMS-0057-F payer-behavior warehouse is starved because W2 CMS grants attestation-driven enforcement discretion — 30-50% payer non-readiness base rate means the API feed is thin into 2028. Crucible's talent raid dents the analytics bench, pushing the build toward the 24-month end of the band.

resolutions.move: Lakeview: renewal-window conversion into signable process rider with Green BATNA
resolutions.rationale: All requested terms pass Gate A, and renewal timing is the one legitimate T1 paper window (3.2). But moves resolve concurrently (3.5) with RegionalMutual's own repricing: outcome is a signed hybrid — Lakeview gets escalation SLAs, quarterly denial-reason reporting, downcode notice-and-documentation; tolling is narrowed to defined windows; RegionalMutual gets its reconsideration ladder and scoped pre-pay clinical-validation rights. Binds at renewal, economics land T2. The Green BATNA read weaker than intended because W2 employers are inertial. Lakeview absorbed the accepted near-term pre-pay tightening during negotiation.

resolutions.move: Prairie: Shared Appeals Utility subscription + Vendor COI addendum demand
resolutions.rationale: Shared services is Prairie's only path inside the friction rules, but the Utility depends on Meridian's slipping build — Prairie holds a subscription and a late-turn pilot, not working capability, so unmanaged-drift physics (3.1: adverse actions +10-20%/18 mo) still bite Prairie this turn. The COI addendum achieved its designed alternate outcome: Crucible refused, the refusal is documented and shared with Green — real leverage banked for T2.

resolutions.move: Summit: gold-card sprint + Direct Access Term Sheets to self-funded employers
resolutions.rationale: Gold-card base rates govern: payer commercial programs are growing (UHC-analog +40% groups) but payer-designed versions cover <20% of PA volume and criteria remain payer-amendable — Summit qualifies several high-volume lines, a small adverse-action-cost improvement only. Employer flank succeeds at exactly pilot scale: two signed 1/1/2028-effective bundles with Green anchors (mutually corroborated by Green's move sheet). Scale claims would have been struck; none were made.

resolutions.move: NationalCo: ASO Pre-Pay Integrity Engine under a PA-retreat flag
resolutions.rationale: Best-executed move of the turn within bounds. The PA retreat is real and nearly free (~$0.05/electronic transaction; pledge-consistent ~11% elimination), and the pre-pay migration exploits the documented market shift (pre-pay ~43% and growing) plus the payer 2-3 year decision-automation lead over providers. Edits-layer deploys fast; contingency fee revenue ramps only small this turn per the 12-18 month curve, with fuller yield T2. Cost: a one-cycle W2 media flare on 'denials that never appear in denial rates' and a growing Green evidentiary file on ASO fee pass-throughs.

resolutions.move: NationalCo/RegionalMutual: multi-year ASO renewal lockdown with controlled transparency
resolutions.rationale: W2 employer inertia (renew absent >8% shock) delivers the mid-market and some non-table jumbos onto 3-year Red-drafted paper — genuine fee-structure shielding through ~2029 on locked accounts. But the coalition anchors, organized this same turn, refused the term, took tolling agreements instead, and issued their own rider into the 2027-28 cycle. Retention index holds; the decisive fight is deferred, not won.

resolutions.move: GovProgramCo: clinician-in-the-loop wrapper + early CMS-0057-F compliance
resolutions.rationale: The legal insulation is real — it addresses the exact surviving theories in Lokken (contract/good-faith) and Kisting-Leung (ERISA fiduciary breach over algorithmic review without medical-director evaluation), and purging volume-linked algorithm documentation removes the most dangerous discovery vector. But in W2 early compliance earns nothing external: CMS extends discretion to everyone, so the moat is defensive only. Clinician sign-off throughput is a real new cost, and the deliberate MA throttle runs medical trend warm through the 2027 measurement year — the priced premium against a Humana-class Stars collapse.

resolutions.move: RegionalMutual: T2 table-setting reprice with Lakeview and Prairie
resolutions.rationale: Resolved jointly with Lakeview's rider into the signed hybrid (see Blue resolution). RegionalMutual secured the metered reconsideration ladder and scoped pre-pay validation rights; paid in transparency reporting, downcode notice, and a published-criteria gold-card charter. The Prairie gold-card offer is nugatory — Texas-pattern volume thresholds (≥5 requests/service/6-month window) structurally exclude a low-volume rural system, consistent with the ~3% statutory uptake base rate.

resolutions.move: Form coalition + issue Green Standard ASO Rider into 2027-28 RFP cycle
resolutions.rationale: Succeeds precisely as scoped: positioning only, zero T1 economics claimed or awarded. The rider passes Gate A intact (all process/fee/data terms). W2 employer inertia limits coalition breadth beyond the anchors, and Red's lockdown removed a slice of the addressable book — but the instrument is in the RFP stream, earliest binding effect T2 per contract-cycle friction, exactly as Green's own assumptions state.

resolutions.move: Vendor COI attestation + independent flat-fee auditor RFP
resolutions.rationale: The attestation cannot be truthfully signed by an entity whose holding company shares a claims-outcome data lake across PI and denial-defense arms; Crucible's refusal is now a documented fiduciary-file fact, Veracity is excluded from direct coalition engagements, and White records the conflict as discoverable and ripening. Cost honestly assessed: the replacement flat-fee auditor is RFP-stage and will be materially less capable than the incumbent through 2027.

resolutions.move: CAA fiduciary pre-litigation posture (demand letters, preservation, tolling fork)
resolutions.rationale: Evidence farming works — preservation demands and the tolling fork landed, with retention-sensitive RegionalMutual cooperating most. But the standing-dismissal pattern (J&J, Wells Fargo) means the threat prices below its headline: NationalCo produces selectively and slow-walks. In W2, no court accelerates this. The file grows; nothing moves a T1 metric, as Green itself predicted.

resolutions.move: Direct-contracting pilots with Summit and Meridian
resolutions.rationale: Summit bundle pilots signed for 1/1/2028 effective dates (corroborated both sheets) — a live, dated, priced exit signal. The Meridian centers-of-excellence carve-out stalls at term-sheet: Meridian's committee physics (12-24 mo cycles) apply to its contracting side too. Pilot scale by design; no scale credit, no scale claimed.

resolutions.move: Veracity PreEmpt: 3-year contingency PI at RegionalMutual and GovProgramCo
resolutions.rationale: Both target archetypes signed — RegionalMutual to close the NationalCo gap (its own SIU freshly thinned by Crucible's raid), GovProgramCo as the price-insensitive buyer under MA margin compression. Recovery yield follows the 12-18 month deployment curve, so revenue is ramp-stage, but 3-year assignable contingency paper at pre-scrutiny rates is banked before Green's terms can bind. Offsetting: the ASO fee pass-through is now a named target in Green's demand letters.

resolutions.move: Bulwark CounterSuit: contingency denial-defense to Blue
resolutions.rationale: Coalition COI discipline gutted table penetration: Prairie chose the Shared Appeals Utility, Lakeview and Meridian walked when Crucible refused the data-segregation addendum. Summit — agile and exposed — signed a limited contingency carve-out despite coalition friction, opening a small intra-Blue seam. Off-table sales to unequipped external providers provide the real growth. The refusal itself is now dual-documented (Blue and Green files).

resolutions.move: ClearRail: CMS-0057-F compliance tollbooth
resolutions.rationale: The move's engine was deadline urgency, and W2 removed it: CMS's attestation/discretion pathway converts January 2027 from forcing function to paperwork. GovProgramCo self-built its ePA APIs (per its own move), NationalCo was never a customer, and uptake shrinks to free-tier connectivity at Prairie and PA-status visibility at Summit. Negative-margin infrastructure with no toll traffic; diffusion base rates already made 2030 infrastructure status unreachable.

resolutions.move: Rule-shaping lobbying + SIU/rev-cycle talent raids
resolutions.rationale: Lobbying is moot in W2 — corridors fail the signability gate on their own, gold-card statutes stall at base rate without help — so no counterfactual win is banked, while the funded-opposition paper trail joins the conflict file. Raids succeed on the labor-market lever and salary asymmetry: RegionalMutual's SIU loss deepens its Veracity dependence (self-serving twice over), and Meridian's bench dent adds schedule friction to the one self-build threatening Bulwark's TAM.

turns.bluePosture: Asymmetric prevention-first race: Blue declines to fight Red claim-by-claim on appeal volume alone (symmetric escalation just inflates admin cost per rule 3.5). Instead we (1) start the 12–24 month build/buy clocks NOW so denial-prevention and agentic-appeals capacity is production-grade by T2, (2) convert Turn-1 renewal windows into signable process terms — SLAs, transparency, audit rights, gold-carding criteria — never numeric corridors, and (3) open a quiet flank toward Green before Green organizes, positioning Blue as the employers' data ally against ASO payment-integrity fee churn. Appeals are prosecuted aggressively in the meantime because base rates favor us (80.7% MA appeal overturn per KFF), but the strategic bet is shrinking preventable denials at the front end, not winning a rework war.

Simultaneously run a preemptive employer-retention lockdown before Green organizes: multi-year ASO renewals sweetened with controlled transparency, traded for preservation of contingency-fee economics. Moderate on fully-insured (MLR rebate leakage makes aggression self-defeating there). Wrap all algorithmic UM in licensed-clinician sign-off to satisfy SB 1120-class laws and blunt the Lokken/PXDX discovery theories. Protect Stars near-term (CTM/appeals measures still bite through the 2027 measurement year), positioning to re-tighten MA UM as those measures sunset for 2029 Stars.

turns.narrative:
The 2028 renewal wall resolved the way employer markets usually resolve: the substance diffused and the standard died. No carrier signed Rider v2 unamended. NationalCo forked it — conceding the audit rights, denial-data feeds, and fee election that give a signing anchor genuine CAA armor, while amputating the hard fee cap and broad clawback — and most tolled anchors, weighing a rate lock against switching disruption and remembering that the CAA standing dismissals make litigation a posture rather than a plan, took the bespoke paper. Green then did the one thing that separates a purchasing coalition from a newsletter: it executed the pre-committed defection, walking one anchor book to a direct-contract-heavy configuration for 1/1/2029. Red's retention index finally moved, and in the wrong direction; Green got most of what its rider demanded without getting its rider.

The operational war is now fully pre-pay, and per doctrine 3.5 the symmetric halves cancelled on headlines while inflating both cells' admin lines: RegionalMutual's clinical-validation program and Meridian's variance engine grind against each other claim by claim, headline denial rates barely twitch, and the disputed dollars churn in a venue no public statistic measures. Meridian's shadow-denial warehouse reached production on owned 835 data — the one feed forbearance could not starve — and Prairie had the cleanest turn on the board: full utility usage, cost per touch down hard, an imaging gold card handed over cheaply by a payer buying home-market quiet. GovProgramCo ran the subtlest move of the game, sequencing UM intensity to the Stars measure sunset with a written no-targets charter built for the discovery it expects.

Crucible lost the turn. Fired by the coalition on a documented fiduciary record, raided by NationalCo's attestation-armed services arm, and pushed out of government-book contingency, it responded rationally — Project Cleave is real, dated, and auditable — but the cure certifies no earlier than mid-2029, and until then the T1 refusals keep pricing it out of both coalitions' front doors. Its locked contingency paper still pays; its growth story stopped.

The environment stayed molasses. CMS extended 0057-F forbearance again, validating Meridian's pivot; Lokken advanced through class-cert briefing without a merits word; a copycat settled sealed and cash-only; the renewal-wall story lived one trade-press cycle; appeal bots reached the high single digits of appeal volume, noticed operationally only in Red's commercial queues. Nothing decided this turn matures before 2029 — which is exactly when everything signed this turn comes due.
env: CMS extends CMS-0057-F enforcement discretion a further 18 months for plans attesting good-faith implementation; trade press covers it, general media does not. Payer API feeds stay thin and late — retroactively validating Meridian's pivot to owned remittance data and further stranding ClearRail's original connectivity thesis. (W2: forbearance regime persists.)

Lokken v. UnitedHealth advances to class-certification briefing; the magistrate compels additional discovery reaching payment-integrity vendor files. No merits ruling. A separate copycat AI-denial action settles confidentially — cash only, sealed, no process commitments, no precedent. (W2 court clocks: 3-5 years to merits; quiet settlements are the mode.)

Kisting-Leung continues on the surviving ERISA fiduciary theory without decision; benefits-bar commentary notes that plan-sponsor demand letters now routinely quote its surviving counts — litigation shaping contracts before it resolves anything.

One-cycle media flare: benefits trade press covers 'the renewal wall' — coalition RFPs, the anchor account that switched carriers, and PI-fee audit clauses. A regional business journal names the moving anchor. No national pickup; the story decays next cycle per W2.

Patient-side appeal AI reaches roughly 6-7% of appeals (from ~4%), still concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members. Overturns track the high base rates; the added queue volume lands hardest on NationalCo and RegionalMutual commercial appeals and on GovProgramCo's narrowed high-dollar denial channel, where IRE overturn counts tick up on lower denial volume.

One additional state enacts an SB 1120-style clinician-determination statute; California issues its first administrative fine under its regime — single digits, against a non-table plan, symbolic. Operationalization lags hold; nothing bites table actors before 2029.

Labor market: Crucible's restructuring pause during Project Cleave cools the vendor salary-premium raids of T1; payer SIU and provider rev-cycle counter-offer inflation moderates, though both sides' T1-inflated admin cost bases persist on the books per doctrine 3.5.

sign.instrument: Downcode & Edit Transparency Schedule (Blue/Lakeview rider amendment)
sign.detail: Machine-readable adverse-action reason codes, notice-and-cure windows, joint operating committee, and reciprocal documentation commitments are checklist items 6, 7, and 10 — process and format terms with no volume or corridor language. turns.narrative:
The final turn is the first in which both principal combatants improved their books by standing down — selectively, and only where the grind had gone negative-yield. The hinge event is an uncoordinated convergence: Lakeview walked into its renewal window carrying a pre-pay reconciliation protocol, and RegionalMutual walked in carrying a nearly identical PA-relief-for-evidence exchange. White consolidated the two drafts into a single signable instrument — the only moment in three turns when opposing cells independently wrote the same paper. The de-escalation is asymmetric by construction: RegionalMutual auto-approves the low-dollar categories it was losing money contesting, retains full pre-pay review on high-dollar DRG and clinical-validation lines, and takes structured clinical evidence at submission in exchange. Both dyads' admin lines deflate for the first time since 2026. Doctrine 3.5 finally ran in reverse — and the Vendor, which had been billing the trench war, is the cell that paid for the peace.

Meridian's prevention offensive landed because it was built two turns ago: the variance engine, past its deployment clock, cut initial denials on targeted code families and was promptly productized through the Utility — a move that incidentally killed Bulwark's white-label pitch the same quarter it was made. Prairie compounded quietly; Summit and the Meridian COE joinder gave Green a full-severity direct network for 1/1/2030. NationalCo answered the one dial it was losing on by administering the defections it could not prevent: the wraparound product brought the walked anchor partway home as a fee-paying administered account, trading contingency PI on those dollars for thinner but clawback-proof PEPM revenue. GovProgramCo ran the coldest play on the board — MA UM intensification timed to the day the Stars complaints, appeals, and disenrollment measures died, wrapped in a no-targets charter built for the discovery it expects and may never face.

Green spent the turn cashing paper rather than proposing it. The fork's true-up clause converted PI fees from earned-on-action to earned-on-outcome, and flat-fee auditors recovered a moderate fraction against the 80-percent-overturn tailwind; the mid-market sweep landed partially, exactly as employer-inertia base rates predicted. Crucible certified Cleave a quarter late, and a quarter is what the exit cost: the cure ripened mid-2030, the coalition front doors reopened with almost no selling time behind them, and Project Bookends launched into a market still pricing Lokken discovery. The environment stayed molasses to the end — class certification denied, forbearance extended past the horizon, appeal bots plateauing near ten percent. The war ended not in victory but in repricing.
env: CMS extends CMS-0057-F enforcement discretion through the end of the scoring horizon for attesting plans and announces discretion will sunset in 2031; trade press covers it, general media does not. The API layer never becomes a forcing function inside the game — Meridian's owned-remittance strategy and ClearRail's stranding are both finalized by the same bulletin. (W2: forbearance to the end.)

Lokken v. UnitedHealth: class certification DENIED as to the nationwide class on predominance; a narrow state-law subclass survives for individual proceedings; no merits ruling by game end. Discovery into PI-vendor files surfaces a pre-Cleave-era Veracity contingency pricing memorandum — one trade-press cycle, then decay, but the document is permanently priced into Vendor exit diligence. (W2 court clocks: class cert usually denied, no precedent accumulates.)

California issues its second clinician-determination enforcement action — a modest fine against a non-table MA plan unable to produce individualized-determination documentation. Trade coverage contrasts it with GovProgramCo's pre-filed UM Integrity Attestation, exactly the affirmative-defense positioning that charter was built for. No table actor is touched. (W2: first enforcement actions are single-digit-scale and symbolic.)

Patient-side appeal AI plateaus at roughly 9-10% of appeals by end-2030 — the top of the W2 band — still concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members. Operational bite lands where denial volume narrowed: IRE overturn counts on GovProgramCo's high-dollar channel rise visibly on shrinking denial counts, an audit-optics fact logged for post-game CMS cycles rather than a scoring event.

One-cycle media flare: benefits trade press runs 'the integrity refund' — coverage of coalition true-up clawbacks forcing carriers to return PI fees on reversed pre-pay actions. One additional non-table jumbo demands fork-floor terms at its renewal; the story decays the following cycle without national pickup. (W2: episodic flares, symmetric decay.)

Labor market: Crucible's separation triggers a final attrition wave — NationalCo's services arm hires the departing Veracity mid-market tail's account teams. The 2026-27 vendor salary-premium era ends, but both sides' inflated admin cost bases from T1 persist on the books through scoring per doctrine 3.5; the arms race's wage bill outlived the arms race.

sign.detail: Wrap-network access, bundle adjudication rails, stop-loss coordination, eligibility/accumulator integration, PEPM fees, no PI contingency on bundle-adjudicated claims — pure fee and process terms in bilateral employer contracts. White notes for the record that a voluntarily filed attestation is also a voluntarily created admission standard if operations ever diverge from it.

signposts: Whether CMS actually enforces 0057-F when discretion sunsets in 2031 — the single event that would drag the pre-pay venue into machine-readable daylight and retroactively revalue every measurement asset in the game (ClearRail's recharter included).

Terms of the eventual Lokken subclass resolutions and whether any settlement ever attaches process commitments — three turns of W2 produced only sealed cash; a single process-term settlement would mark a regime break.

Patient appeal-AI crossing ~15% of appeals or acquiring a statutory tailwind (state-funded appeal assistance, mandated bot-accessible denial data) — either would convert a niche cost into a structural constraint on denial economics.

Whether wraparound administration becomes the carrier industry's standard answer to direct contracting — and whether it functions as the retention tool Red priced or as the adjudication-rail Trojan horse that teaches employers they never needed the carrier relationship, only the rails.
Closing multiples on Project Bookends' two tracks versus the Cotiviti/Machinify comps — the market's verdict on whether exiting the conflict was worth more than operating it.

resolutions.move: First-Pass Yield Offensive (Meridian): variance engine moves pre-submission
resolutions.rationale: Doctrine 3.2 satisfied: warehouse and engine were built T1 and in production T2, so measurable T3 impact is friction-consistent. Denial rate on the Meridian book falls 1-2 pts and cost-per-touch falls 20-30% on targeted families — both inside 3.3 bounds. Prevention beats recovery arithmetically (a denial never issued recovers 100% at near-zero appeal labor vs 55-80% on appeal at full cost). NationalCo took the bilateral mirror only in narrowed, forked form late in the turn, consistent with its documented fork behavior; Red retargeting to new edit families produced one whack-a-mole cycle, detected within a quarter on owned 835 data as claimed.

resolutions.move: Enforce and reprice at the renewal window (Lakeview)
resolutions.rationale: Contract terms bind at renewal (3.2) and this was the dyad's renewal turn. Lakeview's protocol and RegionalMutual's exchange were substantively the same instrument — White consolidated them; per 3.5 this is the cooperative asymmetric route that moves real metrics: disputed-dollar cycle time collapses, timely-filing and abandoned low-dollar write-offs shrink, both admin lines deflate. Notice-and-cure survived in compromised form (60-day notice, cure limited to the annual requalification cycle). The Lakeview direct-contract lane signed regardless, cutting the 45% concentration modestly — the retaliation hostage is being released on Lakeview's schedule.

resolutions.move: Utility deepening and gold-card extension (Prairie)
resolutions.rationale: All three actions are purchases or petitions under signed instruments — no build clock, no scale-claim to strike. Pre-bill hardening subscription converts Meridian's fixed investment into Prairie's variable-cost prevention. RegionalMutual, already exiting low-yield categories unilaterally, granted one rural line immediately and phased the second pending a requalification cycle — consistent with gold-card base rates keeping coverage well under 20% of PA volume. Prairie's dependency risk (Meridian hub + payer-amendable criteria) is real and logged, but the alternative was base-rate drift.

resolutions.move: Direct-access scale-up (Summit)
resolutions.rationale: Doctrine 3.5 names Green-brokered channels as the route to large shifts, and this is Blue's only structurally zero-adverse-action revenue. Honest repricing on published pilot data, dropped underperforming bundles, and the executed Meridian COE joinder gave the channel a full severity range for 1/1/2030. Per VBC base rates (two-sided risk ~2-5 pp/yr, never >5) the channel stays a minority of coalition spend through 2030 — Summit claimed no more. NationalCo's wraparound cut both ways: it validated the channel and made employer adoption operationally easier.

resolutions.move: Wraparound Administration (NationalCo)
resolutions.rationale: The scoring logic is sound — an account that carves out orthopedics but keeps NationalCo rails is retained, not lost — and the walked anchor took wrap administration for 1/1/2030, stabilizing the retention index. But it is administration recovered, not the carrier relationship: PEPM wrap fees are structurally thinner than the contingency PI they replace on carved-out volume, and the product certifies to every wavering anchor that direct contracting is safe to try. Retention improves; the fee mix dilutes; the strategic validation of the exit channel is permanent.

resolutions.move: MA UM normalization timed to the Stars sunset (GovProgramCo)
resolutions.rationale: The regulatory arbitrage is real per the payer economics brief: 2029 Stars (2027 measurement year) delete the CTM/appeals/disenrollment measures that priced UM friction, and electronic review scales at ~$0.05/transaction. Intensification stayed inside the ±2pt bound, every adverse action carried individualized clinician sign-off under the pre-filed no-targets charter, and the KFF appeal base rates (1.6-19.9% appealed) make even 80%+ overturns cheap in expectation. Second-order cost logged: IRE overturn counts rose visibly on the narrowed high-dollar channel as appeal bots concentrated there — audit optics banked for a post-game CMS cycle, not a scoring event under W2.

resolutions.move: Asymmetric de-escalation of negative-yield pre-pay grind (RegionalMutual)
resolutions.rationale: Correct application of 3.5: the T2 symmetric grind cancelled on headlines while paying the Vendor. Auto-approving categories where admin cost exceeded realized recovery cut cost-per-touch inside the ±35% bound and deflated the T1-inflated admin base; concentrating review on high-dollar lines preserved the yield that was real. The Veracity contingency-to-hybrid conversion executed at renewal as pre-negotiated, shrinking the discoverable contingency footprint ahead of Lokken's PI-vendor discovery. The forgone recoveries were negative-yield after appeal labor — the concession cost less than it looked.

resolutions.move: PI fee-yield defense: reprice ahead of the clawback (NationalCo services arm)
resolutions.rationale: The repricing race resolved as a draw with Green: subscription-plus-capped-success and the pre-pay prevention mix shielded the go-forward book (fees on prevented dollars cannot be overturned and clawed), but Green's true-up reconciliation recovered a moderate fraction of 2029 legacy contingency fees on reversed actions — Red's own fork language did the damage. Crucible-window captures were real but time-boxed: the cure ripened mid-2030 and ended the monopoly moment early. Net PI yield holds flat rather than grows — survival of the metric, not expansion.

resolutions.move: Cash the true-up: coalition-wide PI fee reconciliation
resolutions.rationale: Enforcement of executed paper faces no diffusion friction — the fork's true-up clause was already in force 1/1/2029, and the 80.7% overturn base rate is Green's actuarial tailwind. Flat-fee auditors quantified the invisible pre-pay venue against 835 outcomes and recovered a moderate fraction via contract reconciliation; scope disputes deadlocked a tail into queues that outlive the game, exactly as Green priced. NationalCo conceded the mirror-conflict independent verification rather than litigate a retention condition. Recovered fees plus visible (shoppable) admin repricing beats buried contingency — the trade Green said it would take.

resolutions.move: 2029 renewal sweep: rider-as-rubric on the unlocked mid-market
resolutions.rationale: Base rates governed: W2 employer inertia (renew incumbent absent premium shock) meant a material minority of mid-market accounts took incumbent paper over rubric scoring. But where renewals were genuinely contested, fork-floor terms won — carriers cannot argue unsignability of terms they executed at anchor scale — and three-seller competition (services arm, converting Veracity, independents) produced structure concessions the fee-cap fight never did. Partial sweep coverage, full precedent value.

resolutions.move: Direct-contract second wave, sized by pilot data
resolutions.rationale: The COE joinder executed under twice-passed master terms; expansion followed positive pilot lanes and dropped negative ones with the losses documented as prominently as the wins — the fiduciary file's credibility asset. The second anchor walk stayed holstered and priced: fork-floor concessions extracted at renewal tables were worth more than the retention-index damage of walking, given VBC base rates cap the channel's share anyway. Disciplined, bounded, and scored accordingly.

resolutions.move: Fiduciary file completion; litigation held at posture
resolutions.rationale: Correct read of the litigation clocks: no CAA/ERISA theory could mature to collection before scoring (standing dismissals per the brief; W2 courts 3-5 yrs to merits), so the documented prudent process — feeds received, audits run, true-ups demanded, awards reasoned — is the cheapest route to holding fiduciary exposure at low. Quoting Kisting-Leung's surviving counts in letters rather than complaints kept the discovery threat priced into negotiations at near-zero spend.

resolutions.move: Project Cleave certification sprint and same-day cure
resolutions.rationale: The separation performed to White's four pre-stated criteria, but the Big-4 certification slipped one quarter to Q3 2029 — scope expansions plus Lokken discovery reaching pre-Cleave Veracity files mid-audit — pushing the two clean quarters to Q4 2029/Q1 2030 and the cure ripe date to Q2 2030. Both COI instruments executed same-day and the certification published voluntarily; the T1 refusals are cured. But the cure bought roughly two selling quarters before scoring, not four. Structurally complete, commercially late.

resolutions.move: Renewal-wall defense: convert the contingency book (Veracity)
resolutions.rationale: Self-conversion on incumbent paper beat displacement odds where relationships held: a majority of expiring logos converted to hybrid at a material take-rate haircut (within 3.3 pricing bounds), and RegionalMutual's pre-negotiated conversion executed with premium. But the tail fired Veracity on the T1 record before the cure ripened, with NationalCo's attestation-armed arm and flat-fee independents splitting the departures, and the post-cure Employer-Direct relaunch reached Green's front door too late in 2030 to book meaningful coalition ARR before scoring.

resolutions.move: Bulwark becomes the Utility's arms supplier
resolutions.rationale: Overtaken by a simultaneous Blue move: Meridian productized its own variance engine as the Utility Pre-Bill Hardening Subscription this same turn, making Bulwark's white-labeled pre-pay module a redundant purchase of a capability the hub now sells. Meridian's committees declined; the springing contract never sprang — precisely the risk Bulwark's own sheet accepted at 'meaningful probability.' ShadowLedger's non-table community sales continue, but table Blue re-entry is now direct-sales into a market the cooperative undercuts on price.

resolutions.move: Project Bookends — dual-track separated exit
resolutions.rationale: The processes launched Q3 2030 (compressed by the cure slip) off two clean but thin quarters. Buyers exist — PE is still paying platform multiples for PI per the Cotiviti/Machinify comps — but every bid carries a litigation-overhang discount from the surfaced pre-Cleave contingency memo in Lokken discovery, plus the sum-of-parts haircut Vendor accepted. ClearRail's measurement-utility recharter adds genuine strategic garnish to the Veracity track. At game end: two credible processes open, zero closed. Scored as launched, not realized.

turns.bluePosture: Asymmetric de-escalation from a hardened position. Turn 2 proved the symmetric pre-pay grind cancels on headlines while inflating our admin line — that path loses Blue's own victory conditions even when we "win" disputes. T3 pivots the coalition from fighting adverse actions to preventing them: Meridian's production warehouse and variance engine move upstream to pre-submission claim hardening; Lakeview converts its enforcement-desk breach ledger into a pre-pay reconciliation protocol at its 2029-30 renewal window; Prairie and Summit scale the two channels that already showed cost-per-touch and dispute-free revenue gains (the Utility and Green direct contracting). Every move either shrinks the disputed pool, cuts cost per touch, or books revenue outside Red's PI apparatus entirely. We enforce paper we already hold rather than propose new grand standards that the diffusion ledger says cannot mature by 2030.
