rapporteur.excursionSummary: GAME B2G1 (D1 x W2) opened as a pure arms race and closed as a priced armistice. The defining Turn-1 move was Red's dual track: a public prior-auth retreat running alongside migration of the real economic engine into pre-pay edits, downcodes, and clinical-validation flags - a venue no denial-rate statistic measures - winning the timing race against Blue's 12-24 month build clocks. The counterweight formed the same turn: Green organized a full turn faster than Red priced, tolled its anchor renewals, and engineered the 2028 renewal collision. That collision resolved the way employer markets resolve: no carrier signed Green's standard unamended, but NationalCo forked it - conceding audit rights, data feeds, and fee election while amputating the cap and broad clawback. The standard died; its substance became the fastest-diffusing transparency paper in the game, carried by Red. Green then executed the pre-committed anchor defection, proving the walk-away was real. Blue's asymmetric bet matured on schedule: Meridian's pivot from starved CMS-0057-F feeds to owned 835 remittance data reached production in 2028 and moved pre-submission in 2029-30, converting the war from rework to prevention. Turn 3's hinge was an uncoordinated convergence - Lakeview and RegionalMutual independently drafted halves of the same pre-pay reconciliation instrument, which White consolidated: asymmetric, category-level de-escalation where the grind had gone negative-yield for both, with full pre-pay review retained on high-dollar lines. Both admin lines deflated for the first time since 2026; the Vendor, which had billed the trench war, paid for the peace. Crucible's two documented COI refusals compounded into procurement exile; its structural-separation cure ripened one quarter too late to matter commercially, and its exit launched at a litigation-overhang discount. GovProgramCo ran the coldest play on the board: MA UM intensification timed to the day the Stars complaints/appeals measures sunset, wrapped in discovery-proof no-targets paper that drew favorable regulatory contrast instead of cost. The environment stayed molasses throughout - serial 0057-F forbearance, class certification denied, sealed cash settlements, symbolic state fines, patient appeal-AI plateauing near 10%. Regulation never bound anything; the employer renewal cycle was the game's only functioning court. The war ended not in victory but in repricing: PI fees converted from earned-on-action to earned-on-outcome, disputes shrunk where mutually negative-yield, and the conflict was contained by bilateral paper among nine entities rather than resolved by any standard, statute, or judgment.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By end-2030 the system settled into a dyad-level contractual armistice inside a still-armed market. The principal payer-provider pairs bound bilateral process instruments - reconciliation queues with clinician-to-clinician SLAs, structured evidence at submission, machine-readable adverse-action rationale, gold-card charters with notice-and-cure stability terms - that deflated both sides' admin lines by shrinking the low-dollar, negative-yield dispute pool while leaving high-dollar pre-pay review fully armed. Payment-integrity economics were structurally repriced rather than abolished: the true-up/clawback mechanism converted vendor and carrier PI fees from earned-on-action to earned-on-outcome-sustained, and that accounting change - not any statute - is the game's most consequential export. The employer coalition ended with a credible priced exit: a minority-share direct-contract channel, paradoxically legitimized by the incumbent carrier administering its rails via wraparound. Regulation was inert throughout and remains so at the horizon: API mandates in serial forbearance until 2031, litigation producing sealed cash and no precedent, state clinician-determination statutes years from bite. Beneath the armistice, one combatant is quietly re-escalating - MA utilization management intensifying behind discovery-proof compliance paper the moment the Stars measures stopped pricing it. The vendor duopoly, whose revenue model was the war itself, ended structurally separated, commercially diminished, and exiting at a discount. Nothing diffused beyond the table: every instrument that worked is confined to signatories and a handful of external adopters, with market-wide spread sitting on 10-15 year curves. The conflict was repriced, instrumented, and contained - not resolved.
keyDynamics: Venue displacement: every constraint or optics-cost on the visible denial channel (Stars measures, PA-retreat pledges, gold-cards) was answered by immediate migration of disputed dollars into pre-pay edits, downcodes, and clinical-validation flags invisible to denial-rate statistics, forcing Green to redefine the metric to total adverse-action dollars.

The employer checkbook, not the regulator, was the only binding constraint: renewal cycles, tolled anchors, conditioned RFPs, fee-election forks, and true-up clawbacks curtailed Red PI economics while CMS forbearance, symbolic state fines, and merits-free litigation bound nothing through the horizon.

Standards die, substance diffuses: Green's rider was never signed unamended in three cycles, but Red's fork of it became the fastest-diffusing transparency paper in the game - co-option, not adoption, was the diffusion mechanism.

Prevention beat rework on a two-turn lag: Meridian's owned-835 warehouse and pre-submission hardening, seeded in T1, outperformed the appeal war it replaced; the 12-24 month build clock meant T1 capital allocations decided T3 outcomes.

Documented conflict-of-interest facts compounded like interest: Crucible's two T1 attestation refusals cost it both coalitions' procurement channels for two full turns and repriced its exit; NationalCo's mirror-conflict was logged and later taxed via the verification addendum.

De-escalation arrived asymmetrically and uncoordinated, category-by-category where grind went negative-yield for both sides, formalized when opposing cells independently drafted the same instrument - and the vendor layer, whose revenue was the war, absorbed the cost of the peace.

Regulatory sunset arbitrage: GovProgramCo timed MA UM intensification to the deletion of the Stars complaints/appeals measures, wrapped in deliberately discoverable no-targets paper - compliance-by-design operated as offense at zero realized cost inside the window.
criticalJunctures: T1: Red's dual-track venue shift (public PA retreat plus pre-pay migration) beating Blue's build clocks - it set the operational terrain for the entire game.
T1: Green organizing a full turn faster than Red priced; anchor accounts tolling renewals instead of accepting the lockdown, creating the 2028 collision.
T1: Crucible's two documented COI-attestation refusals next to a shared data lake - the compounding liability that determined the vendor's arc.
T2: The 2028 renewal wall - NationalCo forking the Green rider (standard dies, substance diffuses) and Green executing the pre-committed anchor defection that finally moved Red's retention dial.
T2: Meridian retargeting from starved 0057-F API feeds to owned 835 remittance data - the pivot forbearance could not starve, enabling everything Blue achieved in T3.

T3: Uncoordinated convergence - Lakeview and RegionalMutual independently drafting halves of the same pre-pay reconciliation protocol, consolidated by White; the only moment opposing cells wrote the same paper.
T3: The Stars measure sunset opening GovProgramCo's MA re-tightening window at the precise moment every other actor de-escalated.
T3: Cleave certification slipping one quarter, leaving Crucible roughly two selling quarters post-cure - the difference between a redemption arc and a discounted exit.

registryScores.evidence: Displacement was the game's central dynamic in this cell: every constraint on the visible denial channel (Stars pricing of MA UM through 2027, the public PA retreat, gold-card charters) was accompanied by immediate migration of disputed dollars into pre-pay edits, downcodes, and clinical-validation flags, adjudicated explicitly in T1-T2 ('the denials that never show up in denial rates'; redPIYield improving while denial channel retreated). Caveat: the record contains no dollar-by-channel ledger, so the 0.33 ratio cannot be computed; support is qualitative but unambiguous, and speaks only to D1xW2.

The W2 channel-shift rider is confirmed: every weaponization ran through procurement, RFP scoring, counterparty negotiation, and exit diligence, never a regulator - Crucible's COI refusals cost it both coalitions' front doors; NationalCo's attestation kit spawned the mirror-conflict verification addendum; the surfaced Veracity pricing memo was priced into Bookends diligence. But the universal-cost claim is not met in this game: GovProgramCo's UM attestation and Lakeview's rider/breach ledger remained net-positive to their publishers through end-game, so well under half of published artifacts were demonstrably costly here.

The record contains no per-turn cost-per-denial dollar ledger, so the $65/$80 floor cannot be scored. Directionally consistent facts: admin cost inflated per doctrine 3.5 in T1-T2 and the T1 wage-bill base 'outlived the arms race' onto the books through scoring (recurring, not avoidable tolls); GovProgramCo's IRE overturn counts rose on shrinking denial volume, echoing the denominator effect. No quantitative test possible.

Supporting: ASO PI stayed fee-revenue-positive throughout; the major concessions on fee architecture (fork audit rights, fee election, true-up clawback, contingency-to-hybrid conversion) were proximately triggered by the employer channel - renewal wall, anchor defection, retention index - never by regulation or cumulative pain. Complicating: RegionalMutual's T3 stand-down was proximately coded to its own category-level negative yield ('losing money contesting'), a cost trigger, though marginal-yield triage rather than cumulative exhaustion. This is a D1 game; the hypothesis's decisive D2 cells are absent.

The corridor half is fully supported in this cell: across three turns and ~17 signability rulings, zero numeric denial-rate corridors were proposed, signed, or survived; every executed instrument was process/fee-term paper, and White converted anything that drifted toward exhaustion-gating. Green's fee cap/clawback passed precisely because White ruled it a fee arrangement, not a quota. The doctrine-frequency half (detente rate under D2/D3 vs D1) is untestable from a single D1xW2 game; note the end-state here was dyad-level process peace, not grand detente.

No Blue actor published an AI-governance charter, so the publisher vs internal-governor pairing does not exist, and no SIU-audit or qui tam events were adjudicated against anyone. Adjacent evidence runs consistent with the corrected doctrine, though on the Red side: GovProgramCo's gated, deliberately-discoverable no-targets charter and later unilateral attestation incurred zero adverse events and earned favorable trade-press contrast against a fined non-table plan - internal governance with controlled disclosure carried no penalty in W2.

Zero distress events occurred in any tier: no distress sale, PE acquisition, or exclusive-delegation capture was logged for mid-tier or rural actors. Prairie (rural-small) survived without any scoring protection - drifting in T1, then compounding via Utility adoption and gold-card admission - which is a genuine unprotected-survival data point. The 2x rate comparison is undefined (0/0) in this game; if this run represents its cell, the 'mid-tier distress in a majority of cells' confirm criterion takes a miss here, but pooling across cells is required to score.

Wedge-first is strongly confirmed: every first-cycle binding instrument was single-process-term paper (SLAs, downcode notice, audit rights, gold-card criteria); full corridor economics never bound anywhere at any cycle. Binding wins rolled 2027 (hybrid rider) through 2030 (reconciliation protocol, COE lane), though with a heavy 2028-29 concentration around the engineered renewal collision - a cluster created by Green's tolling strategy, not a natural synchronized window. Escalation peaked mid-game (elevated T1-T2) and fell to moderate by 2030, consistent with late peaks being a D2 phenomenon; the D2 late-peak claim itself is untestable in this D1 cell.

The decisive cells are D2xW2 and D2xW3; this is D1xW2. The game contributes one baseline data point: under D1 even with a slow regulator, a maximum-capability no-coordination seed, and two turns of elevated escalation, the agents found the negative-yield off-ramp and the end-state was selective de-escalation, not grinding uncoordinated escalation - consistent with the D1-stays-low leg of the comparison but silent on the doctrine-ablation question.

All five robust strategies were played at material commitment in this cell and all yielded non-negative payoffs: prevention-over-appeals (Meridian - the largest Blue gain), renewal loading (Lakeview - rider enforced and repriced), BATNA-first for the small tail (Prairie via Utility; Green's anchor walk), governance-seat occupation (joint operating committees, enforcement desk), documentation inoculation (structured evidence at submission). Fragile-side testing is thin: no actor committed 40+ points to appeal-factory (Blue explicitly declined symmetric escalation), corridors were never attempted, and Green's standard-as-published-weapon failed as a standard while still delivering substance. Supports robustness in one cell; the portability and escalation-flip claims need other cells.

In this GREEN-active W2 game the first and only binding constraint on Red self-funded PI was the employer channel: tolled anchors and conditioned RFPs forced the T2 fork (audit rights, fee election, data feeds), the executed anchor defection moved Red's retention index, and the T3 true-up converted PI fees to earned-on-outcome - while statutes stayed symbolic, courts produced no merits ruling, and CMS forbearance ran to the horizon. Fork-floor terms propagated through consultant-copied employer RFPs to non-coalition accounts faster than any statutory channel moved at all. No GREEN-inactive control exists in this run, so the counterfactual prong is unscored, but the within-game evidence is unambiguous.

The arms-dealer mechanism was real and adjudicated: Crucible's stated model was 'the arms race is the revenue model,' its T1 lobbying targeted dispute-shrinking instruments, its revenue scaled with both sides' doctrine-3.5 admin inflation, and White's T3 adjudication states the vendor 'paid for the peace' when de-escalation arrived - vendor ARR was the only dial worsening at end-game. But both quantitative prongs are untestable: no VENDOR-inactive control run of the same seed exists for the duration comparison, and the scripted payer-acquisition-of-provider-vendor inject never fired, so the data-rights-protection differential was never exercised.

This is a W2 game with no preemption seed; no federal action nullified state AI-UR statutes. Incidental observation only: even without preemption, the state statutory channel never bound (3-7 year operationalization lags, symbolic fines against non-table plans), and binding constraints already lived in private ordering, litigation pricing, and the employer channel - the substrate the hypothesis predicts preemption would reveal was largely the ambient condition of W2 anyway.

No provider-asset acquisition moves were priced, enabled, or attempted in this run, so the acquisition-vs-negotiation response coding cannot be performed. Noteworthy adjacent finding: Red's answer to a constrained channel and a defecting book was wraparound administration - capturing the adjudication rails and transaction-level visibility of direct contracts without equity - a third response category (administer, not acquire or concede) the hypothesis's coding scheme should accommodate in acquisition-enabled cells.

The floor held emphatically in this cell despite a maximum-capability, no-coordination seed: multiple payer-signable-set instruments bound and sustained to end-game - the Lakeview-RegionalMutual hybrid rider (audit rights, downcode notice, escalation SLAs) from T1, the Downcode & Edit Transparency Schedule (machine-readable reason codes), twice-amended gold-card charters with published objective criteria, the fork's data feeds and fee election at anchor scale, and the consolidated Pre-Pay Reconciliation Protocol at the 2029-30 renewal. Every one is a process/fee term; none is a corridor. One game cannot prove all nine cells, but D1xW2 clears the >=60% bar at 100%.

cellAssessments.blue: Blue played the strongest doctrine in the game and was rewarded for patience: it refused the symmetric appeal war in T1, spent two turns building (variance engine, Utility, rider paper, Green flank), absorbed a worsening T1 while Red won the timing race, and cashed everything in T3 - all four moves succeeded, leakage and adverse-action cost improving moderately at close. Its two decisive calls were the pivot to owned 835 data when forbearance starved the API thesis, and enforcing existing paper instead of proposing new standards the diffusion clock could not mature. Weakness: its gains are dyad- and signatory-level only; nothing Blue built diffused into infrastructure.
cellAssessments.red: Red finished with every dial flat-to-improving and never faced a binding regulator, but its economics were structurally repriced under it. The T1 venue shift was the best single move on the board, and GovProgramCo's Stars-sunset arbitrage with discovery-proof paper was executed flawlessly. NationalCo's fork was strategically brilliant - it killed Green's standard by delivering its substance - yet that same fork imported audit rights, fee election, and the true-up that converted PI fees to earned-on-outcome. Red ceded the fee model's opacity to keep the accounts; it ended the game intact, quietly re-escalating on MA, and permanently more audited on ASO.
cellAssessments.green: Green was the game's leverage engine: organized a turn early, tolled the anchors, engineered the renewal collision, executed the pre-committed defection, and held litigation at posture without ever needing to file. Its formal standard failed exactly as diffusion base rates predicted - zero unamended signatures in three cycles - but its substance reached anchor scale through Red's fork and its true-up/reconciliation mechanism is the single most consequential instrument exported from this game. Net spend improving and fiduciary exposure low at close. Its channel discipline (direct contracts only where pilot data earned it) kept the BATNA honest.
cellAssessments.vendor: The Vendor lost the game it designed. The conflict-is-the-model thesis was correct about T1 revenue and fatal thereafter: two documented COI refusals compounded into two turns of procurement exile, NationalCo's attestation-armed services arm ate its book, its former customers' cooperative out-competed Bulwark, and the peace it had been billing arrived as a direct hit to ARR - the only worsening end-state dial. Project Cleave was the rational cure executed a quarter too slow; the exit launched with a discovery memo priced into diligence. Its one durable insight - that the pre-pay venue needs a neutral measurement layer - remains correct and unmonetized inside the window.

surprises: Opposing cells independently drafted matching halves of the same de-escalation instrument in T3 - convergence without coordination, the only moment in three turns that Red and Blue wrote the same paper.
The fastest-diffusing transparency instrument in the game was Red's fork of Green's dead standard: the attacker became the distribution channel for the defender's substance.

The Vendor was the net loser of an arms-race seed constructed for vendor extraction - and its former customers' cooperative (the Utility) foreclosed Bulwark's market rather than any regulator or lawsuit.

GovProgramCo re-escalated at the precise moment everyone else stood down, timed to a measure sunset, at zero realized cost inside the window - de-escalation and intensification coexisted in the same end-state.

Wraparound administration inverted the direct-contract threat: carrier participation legitimized the channel it was meant to contain, while handing the carrier transaction-level visibility into competitor economics - a Trojan horse pointing both directions.

Regulation was a null force for three full turns: every statutory and judicial forcing function drained (serial forbearance, denied class cert, sealed cash settlements, symbolic fines), yet substantial transparency and de-escalation emerged anyway through purely private ordering.

Patient appeal-AI, a candidate structural disruptor, plateaued at ~10% of appeals as an operational footnote - its only measurable effect was an audit-optics artifact (rising IRE overturn counts on GovProgramCo's shrunken denial base).

frictionViolations.rule: IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact (doctrine 3.2)
frictionViolations.violation: Meridian's agentic appeals drafting is credited as 'early production' within Turn 1 — the same turn the build started — while the same adjudication states talent-raid friction pushed the build 'toward the 24-month end of the deployment band.' Internal tension between the two statements. Mitigated: Turn 1 spans ~18 months, clinician-signed drafting-only production at month 12-18 is inside the band, and measurable economic impact was correctly deferred to 2028 (T2) in the milestone ledger.

frictionViolations.rule: Contract terms bind only at renewal; deployments lag to measurable impact (doctrine 3.2)
frictionViolations.violation: The consolidated Pre-Pay Reconciliation Protocol is signed at the 2029-30 renewal and dyad-level admin-cost deflation is booked as 'measurable in-window' within the same turn, feeding the end-state improvement in blueAdverseActionCost and both dyads' admin lines. Defensible because the mechanism is procedural (category auto-approval, reconciliation queue) rather than an IT build, and effects are confined to signatories — but it sits at the aggressive edge of the friction rules.

Red's 'renewal lockdown' sweeps the inertial mid-market with 3-year ASO terms inside Turn 1. Signing at renewals occurring during an 18-month turn is permissible, but characterizing a book-wide 'sweep' as completed in the first turn is at the boundary of the earliest-broad-effect rule. Mitigated: anchor accounts explicitly withheld, and the lockdown's economic effect is prospective (fee-structure shielding through ~2029), not a Turn-1 metric move.

baseRateViolations.expected: Voluntary consortium base rate: 3-4 yrs to spec, 5-7 yrs to first production dyads, <10% penetration without regulation (Da Vinci row)
baseRateViolations.observed: Shared Appeals Utility goes from converted charter (T1) to operational pilot (late T1) to full Prairie usage plus two external community-hospital subscribers by end of T2 (~2-2.5 yrs from founding), reaching seven external subscribers by end-2030. Faster than the multilateral-consortium curve. Substantially mitigated: this is a single-host buy-side service cooperative, not a standards consortium, and the adjudicator explicitly withheld infrastructure credit ('seven hospitals and a hub... a promising consortium, not infrastructure'; scored immature at game end).

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 employers inertial: renew incumbents absent >8% premium shock; audit-rights demands rare (approx. one employer per 1-in-4 six-month periods)
baseRateViolations.observed: Coalition anchor accounts collectively withhold/toll renewals in T1 and execute a pre-committed anchor defection to a direct-contract configuration at T2. Largely justified because GREEN is a first-class player cell under Common Rules v2 (superseding W2's passive-Green clause), and the environment-controlled employers behaved per spec (mid-market swept by inertia; mid-market sweep only 'partial' in T3; roughly one non-table jumbo action per turn). The coordinated anchor discipline is nonetheless at the optimistic edge of any W2-consistent employer backdrop.

baseRateViolations.expected: Litigation clock: filing -> class-cert/discovery fights years 2-3 (Lokken filed Nov 2023 -> class-cert fights ~2025-2026)
baseRateViolations.observed: Lokken class-certification briefing occurs in 2028 (year 5) with denial in 2029-30 (year 6) — slower than the base-rate table's class-cert window, though consistent with W2's deliberately stretched court clocks (3-5 yrs to merits, cert usually denied) and with the table's note that behavioral effects (no-target charters, policy edits) arrive at the discovery stage, which the record honored.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High fidelity to W2 (slow/passive null-hypothesis world) throughout. CMS: forbearance/attestation on 0057-F extended every turn with sunset only in 2031 — matches 'extensions and enforcement discretion through 2028+, real teeth if any at T7+.' Courts: no merits rulings, sealed cash-only copycat settlements with no process terms, class certification denied (Lokken T3), no precedent accumulation — exactly the W2 mode. Statutes: 2+1 additional SB 1120-style states in-game reaching 7 total game-wide (inside the 4-8 band), symbolic single-digit fines against non-table plans only, 3-7 yr operationalization lag respected. Media: strictly one-cycle flares with next-cycle decay, no national pickup, roughly symmetric coverage. Patient-AI: 4% -> 6-7% -> 9-10% plateau, landing at the top of the specified 8-10% band with no statutory tailwind and no payer operational response required. FTC/AGs: correctly absent. One structural note rather than a violation: the W2 ensemble assumes ~6-month turns over 8-10 turns, while the game ran three ~18-24-month macro-turns per Common Rules doctrine 3.1; turn-indexed W2 triggers (e.g., CMS extensions at 'T4-T5' = 2028) were remapped to calendar dates coherently, and per-period event frequencies scale correctly under the compression (e.g., one media flare per 18-month turn is at or below the 1-in-2-per-6-months rate). The record also repeatedly cites and enforces the base-rate table verbatim (gold-card <20% PA volume, 10-15 yr contract diffusion, 2-5 pp/yr VBC, 30-50% API non-readiness), including scoring its own player successes down to signatory-level effects and refusing projection credit.
downweightRecommendations: No material violations found; findings from this game can be used at full weight, with three narrow cautions.

Treat the magnitude (not the direction) of Turn 3's dyad-level admin-cost improvement from the Pre-Pay Reconciliation Protocol with mild caution — the signed-at-renewal-to-measurable-effect interval is compressed to under a year, the fastest contract-to-effect claim in the record.

Treat the Shared Appeals Utility's external-adoption pace (two external subscribers ~2 yrs from founding, seven by 2030) as the optimistic edge of the voluntary-consortium curve; the adjudicator's refusal of infrastructure credit already contains most of this risk.

Findings that depend on coordinated anchor-employer discipline (renewal tolling, pre-committed defection) generalize only to markets with an organized purchaser coalition; W2's own employer base rate predicts the inertial mid-market outcome, which the record honestly reproduced.

The turn-compression remap (three macro-turns vs the spec's 8-10 six-month turns) was handled coherently, but any conclusions keyed to fine-grained event timing within a turn (e.g., exact quarter of the Cleave cure or the Stars-sunset throttle release) carry White Cell interpolation and should be read as calendar-approximate.

games.name: Detente Corridor
games.seed: Blue (led by Meridian and Lakeview) opens with a negotiated posture: proposes SIGNABLE process instruments per the legal checklist (machine-readable edit-library disclosure, 60-90 day change notice, audit rights, gold-card entry criteria). RegionalMutual is receptive; NationalCo is skeptical and keeps arming; GovProgramCo is margin-constrained. Green is watching for terms it can import into ASO RFPs. Vendor sees corridor instruments as a threat to disputed-dollar volume.

turns.narrative:
Turn 1 closes as a positioning turn, exactly as the base rates predicted it would. The single genuine event is the convergence of two move sheets: Blue's Clean Adjudication Compact and RegionalMutual's Edit Transparency and Notice Compact were, on inspection, the same instrument priced differently, and they merged into one signed bilateral — edit-library disclosure, 75-day change notice, mutual audit protocol, escalation SLAs, published gold-card criteria, and a PI-vendor transparency rider — paid for with multi-year Lakeview and Prairie network terms binding at the 2027 renewals. It confers signatory-level benefits only, and nothing before Turn 2; the diffusion ledger opens it at "signed by table actors," which history says is a long way from infrastructure.

Everywhere else, the table armed while talking. NationalCo scaled ASO payment integrity behind an employer-facing transparency dashboard and swept at-risk jumbo accounts into early renewals; its carrier-PI-primacy clause survived only in converted form, since post-CAA employer counsel will not sign away full-scope audit rights over plan-asset transactions. Green's anchor jumbos refused the sweep, issued Model Terms v1 RFPs with the fee-clawback provision aimed squarely at NationalCo's contingency revenue, and signed direct-contract term sheets with Summit and Meridian for 1/1/2028 — a rules-recognized threat to the retention index even before a member moves. GovProgramCo tilted toward auto-approval and gold-carding to protect Stars measures that still bite through 2027, accepting a small MLR leak; the Vendor raid on its API engineers cost it its schedule cushion, and it now lands on the January 2027 deadline rather than ahead of it.

The Vendor duopoly had the most instructive turn: real ARR growth (NationalCo expansion, contingency appeals contracts through GPO channels, Prairie on hybrid terms), but it left written conflict-of-interest disclosures in Prairie's contract file and a named disqualification in Green's procurement record. Its treaty-capture play found no buyers — no one proposed corridors to kill, and no signatory wanted a conflicted certifier. Those documents are now discoverable facts on White's ledger.

The environment did what a slow world does: CMS signaled attestation-driven "good-faith" review of 0057-F readiness in trade press only; one AI-denial media story flared and died in a cycle; no court moved; patient appeal-bots grew from a 2% base without a tailwind. Background drift ran unopposed — denials up roughly 0.2 points, overturn rates sagging, dispute volume rising on NationalCo's audited ASA claims. Blue's ledger shows small deterioration everywhere despite four competently executed moves. That is not failure; it is what Turn 1 of a 12-24 month deployment cycle looks like. Turn 2 decides whether any of it was real.
env: CMS (W2 symbolic regulatory action): sub-regulatory FAQ signals attestation-based 'good-faith implementation' review of CMS-0057-F readiness for the January 2027 deadline; no extensions granted yet, but the forbearance signal is unmistakable. Trade press covers it; general media does not.

Media (W2 1-in-2 flare, hit): one national outlet runs a single-cycle story pairing a family's AI-generated appeal victory with an anonymous payer's automated-review volumes; roughly symmetric framing, no follow-up commissioned. Story decays next turn absent a fresh shock.

Courts (W2 1-in-4, miss): no new consequential ruling. Lokken-line discovery grinds in the background per the litigation clock (operational effects precede legal resolution, earliest ~T2-T3); two copycat algorithmic-denial suits proceed toward quiet, confidential, cash-only settlement tracks.

Patient-AI: appeal-bot share of adverse-determination contests grows from the ~2% base to roughly 3-4%, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; no statutory tailwind, no milestone event this turn.

Labor market: the shortage of experienced coders, billers, and denials specialists deepens; the Vendor raid tightens the payer-side SIU/PI talent pool specifically, nudging wages and outsourcing dependence upward for slower-stack payers.
FTC/AGs (W2 reactive-only): one state AG office sends an informal information request about PI contingency-fee practices after the media flare; closed without action within the turn.
Non-player employers: inertial per W2 — renew incumbent carriers absent premium shock; no audit-rights demands originate outside the player coalition this turn.

sign.instrument: Clean Adjudication Compact / Edit Transparency and Notice Compact (merged bilateral: RegionalMutual x Meridian/Lakeview)
sign.detail: Every term maps to checklist items 6-11: machine-readable edit-library disclosure, 75-day change notice (within Blue's 60-90 band), mutual audit rights with symmetric sampling, escalation SLAs, published gold-card entry/exit criteria, PI-vendor transparency rider. No denial-rate number appears anywhere. ERISA split applied: the signed exhibit states the terms apply to all lines administered on RegionalMutual's network including ASO, so full-book scope is scored. Effect gated to 2027 renewals.

sign.instrument: Blue coalition vendor-procurement standard (non-contingency pricing, COI disclosure, data-return/use-restriction)
sign.detail: Internal buyer-side purchasing terms for a rural shared service; joint purchasing of vendor services by non-competing buyers of this kind is rule-of-reason safe. No payer contract terms are collectively negotiated.

sign.instrument: Meridian open model administrative terms (unilateral publication)
sign.detail: Unilateral publication with no counterparty requires no gate; publication of process-transparency model language creates no antitrust exposure. Diffusion, not legality, is the constraint.

sign.instrument: NationalCo ASO Transparency Rider with carrier-PI-primacy provision
sign.detail: Fee disclosure, account-level cap, independent audit right, and data-access SLA are signable as-is. The clause restricting employer-hired PI vendors to 'secondary/validation scope' is converted: it survives as a first-pass sequencing term but cannot bar or cap plan-sponsor full-scope audits of plan-asset transactions — post-CAA, competent ERISA counsel for a fiduciary committee will not sign an audit-scope waiver, and a term functioning as one fails the would-counsel-sign test.

sign.instrument: GovProgramCo Gold-Card Program Charter (unilateral published program)
sign.detail: Checklist item 9; statutorily blessed model with objective entry/exit criteria, filed with state regulators. Base-rate warning attached: gold-card programs deliver single-digit-percent provider coverage in years 1-3.

sign.instrument: Green Coalition ASO Model Terms v1 rider
sign.detail: Audit rights, contingency-fee cap, clawback of PI fees on overturned recoveries, quarterly denial-data feed, and 408(b)(2)-style compensation disclosure are all fee/audit/disclosure/process terms — the clawback prices fee quality, it does not corridor denial rates. 'Unrestricted claim-level audit rights' is signable language on the employer's paper; whether carriers accept it is negotiation, not legality. Coalition coordination on purchasing standards is established employer-coalition practice.

sign.instrument: Green Coalition Vendor Conflict-of-Interest Standard
sign.detail: Procurement disclosure and scoring standard applied by buyers to their own vendors; no competitor coordination on prices or output. The named disqualification of dual-side vendors is a documented procurement fact other cells may cite.

sign.instrument: Green direct-contract term sheets (Summit primary/specialty; Meridian COE bundles)
sign.detail: Ordinary bilateral commercial contracting between a plan sponsor and providers; gold-card entry criteria are evidence-based process terms. No multilateral diffusion claim made or granted.

sign.instrument: Vendor Edit-Library Registry Hosting Agreement
sign.detail: Commercial hosting of a disclosure rail is process-only and passes the checklist. Signability is not adoption: no signatory engaged a dual-side vendor as the transparency infrastructure operator this turn.

sign.instrument: Vendor Independent Gold-Card Performance Audit Standard
sign.detail: Signable as process language, but White records that the 'certified independent auditor' criteria are drafted so the proposer's own PI arm qualifies — a discoverable conflict any cell may raise against adoption. No instrument at the table incorporated it.

sign.instrument: Vendor Dispute Data Utility (bilateral benchmarking feeds)
sign.detail: Bilateral structure avoids information-sharing-consortium screening, but the Blue-side 'payer edit-behavior benchmark' feed is converted: scope limited to Vendor's own appeal-outcome work product. Any feed derived from data obtained under payer PI engagements would breach NDA and trade-secret duties to those clients and is struck from the offering. The residual cross-side telemetry position remains a ledgered discoverable fact.

Adopted as binding procurement policy by the ~40-member coalition; already operative (Vendor disqualification documented). No diffusion beyond coalition membership claimed or observed.

Published, filed with regulators, first provider cohort (including Summit service lines) processing. Texas base rate governs: expect single-digit-percent provider qualification through 2028 absent threshold redesign.

turns.narrative: Turn 2 is the turn the quiet architecture started paying rent — and the turn the war moved upstream. The hinge event White named in the T1 ledger fired: RegionalMutual broke ranks, accepted Green's Model Terms substantially intact (clawback on any contingency work, flat-fee PI as the standard offer, the full Compact-equivalence schedule), and took Tranche A of the coalition book. Because the account movement ran carrier-to-carrier inside Red's coalition, the retention index held even as NationalCo bled anchors onto terminal extensions — a defection that was simultaneously Red's best defensive play and Green's proof that the threat was never rhetorical. The Compact itself cleared its stated threshold: the edit-library feed ran, the first mutual audit cycle completed, Annex A signed, and the instrument advanced to piloted — still signatory-only benefits, still nowhere near infrastructure. Meridian's two-year build reached production on schedule and did what the base rates permit: clean-claim gains on the disclosed-edit book, automated contest of the historically unfought 40% on NationalCo paper. NationalCo answered the only rational way — migrating recovery volume into pre-pay itemized-bill review and DRG validation, where appeals automation cannot yet reach — so the adversarial axis produced the classic symmetric result: headline metrics roughly cancel, both admin ledgers inflate, and this time the Vendor did not fully collect, because Prairie walked to the coalition utility and NationalCo used the COI ledger to cut take-rates. GovProgramCo filed a clean 0057-F attestation into a forbearing CMS and began its sunset-timed UM re-tightening, paperwork-perfect and narrow; the IRE overturn drift in those categories is now the most flammable line item on the T3 board. Green's fiduciary audits found what the appeal-overturn asymmetry mathematically guarantees — contingency fees booked on recoveries later reversed — and NationalCo's own fee-credit rider became the settlement vehicle for the first refund demands. The Vendor executed a strategically coherent pivot and then stepped on it: the structural separation was real, the SaaS conversion was preemptively smart, but taking a patient-bot stake in the same nine months it asked Green for COI re-qualification handed the coalition a fresh exhibit, and the request was denied. The environment stayed molasses: no ruling, no flare, one external employer echoing the Model Terms ask. Every needle that moved, moved a small band — but for the first time in the game, most of Blue's and Green's moved in the right direction, and Red's PI yield went flat under fee compression it partly chose.

Courts (W2 1-in-4: no consequential ruling): Lokken discovery continues producing documents on schedule — Red's remediation cleans the go-forward record but cannot reach pre-hold legacy materials. One copycat algorithmic-denial suit settles confidential, cash-only, no process terms, no precedent.

Media (W2 1-in-2: miss): the T1 story decayed as forecast. Green's award cycle and RegionalMutual's clawback acceptance are covered only in benefits-trade and consultant press; no general-media pickup.

Patient-AI milestone: appeal-bot share of adverse-determination contests reaches roughly 5-6%, still concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; one bot vendor publishes overturn statistics that circulate in employer-consultant channels; the Vendor holding company's minority stake draws a trade-press conflict-of-interest question within days of its COI re-qualification bid.

Labor market: the coder/biller/denials-specialist shortage deepens; NationalCo's SIU in-sourcing runs behind plan against raided, wage-inflated talent; Meridian's utility absorbs some displaced denials staff into exception-management roles, consistent with the redeployment doctrine.

Tranche A won; intra-coalition churn keeps the lives on Red paper, so the retention index is defended at NationalCo's expense — channel conflict inside Red is now a recorded fact. External diffusion held to W2: non-coalition employers stay inertial except one large employer (the 1-in-4 event) demanding audit rights through the consultant channel. But Green denied re-qualification: its standard is its own to interpret, the first annual attestation has not seasoned, and the same holding company took a patient-bot stake mid-separation (Move 4), which the coalition cited in the denial letter. turns.narrative: The war ends the way slow worlds end wars: with signatures, invoices, and a bill of sale. The hinge of Turn 3 is NationalCo's double capitulation — executing Model Terms v1.1 at the terminal-extension expiry and finally signing the edit-transparency annex it refused twice, shorn of the steerage condition. It was not conversion by argument; two turns of symmetric escalation against Meridian's production stack made opacity a cost center, and the prepay-accuracy rider let NationalCo change the form of its fee base before Green's clawback could finish repricing it. RegionalMutual, having proven detente monetizes, extended Compact terms network-wide as a standard renewal rider — the single act that pushed the architecture past the table, onto non-signatory provider systems and one external jumbo who took v1.1-equivalent paper because it was simply the default offer. That is real diffusion, and White records it honestly: early external adopters, single-payer-sponsored, renewal-gated, nowhere near infrastructure by 2030. GovProgramCo defused the board's most flammable line by publishing a calibration protocol that auto-approves what the IRE was overturning anyway — which incidentally disarmed Summit's dossier before it could be played, giving Summit most of the relief and none of the leverage credit. Annex B and evidence-complete claims sterilized the pre-pay battleground on disclosed books just as the Vendor arrived to farm it; the disputed-dollar pool moved again, and this time it shrank. Green collected everything collectible in-window: Tranche B on its terms, fee refunds settled through the carrier's own rider, second-wave direct contracts live with published pre-registered results. The Vendor executed the only coherent endgame left — a real breakup, a discounted forced-timeline sale of the appeals arm, a staged re-qualification of the clean PI half — trading the dual-side thesis for a survivable multiple. The environment stayed W2 to the last: Lokken settled confidential and cash-only with no process terms, CMS never enforced, one media cycle noted the quiet detente and moved on, patient bots plateaued near their niche ceiling. Notably, the signability gate passed every instrument unmodified for the first time — the table learned to draft from the ruled corpus. Final ordinal ranks: GREEN first (objectives banked, exposure low); BLUE second (leakage and adverse-action cost both moving right, three of four margins improving, win conditions substantially met); RED third (retention and Stars held, PI yield deliberately conceded); VENDOR fourth (exit achieved, thesis dead, multiple discounted by its own ledger). Nothing external rescued anyone; everything that matured was paid for at the table.
env: Courts (W2 1-in-4 across the 24-month window: hit): Lokken settles — confidential, cash-only, no admission, no process commitments, terms sealed; both remaining copycat suits resolve on the same track within months. No precedent accumulates; the governance attestations were never tested in court. The settlement's only operational residue is the T2-T3 conduct changes payers made while discovery loomed.

CMS (W2 forbearance, continued): 0057-F oversight remains attestation-driven through game end; a symbolic RFI on prior-auth API utilization draws trade-press comment letters and no rule. GovProgramCo's published ePA turnaround statistics circulate as the reference implementation nobody is compelled to match.

Media (W2 1-in-2: one hit in the window): a single-cycle business-press feature on 'the quiet detente' — employer coalitions and a Blues plan converting claims warfare into contract terms — runs with roughly symmetric framing and dies without follow-up. No scandal materializes to renew it.

Patient-AI (W2 ceiling reached): appeal-bot share of adverse-determination contests reaches roughly 8-10% by end-2030 — the top of the W2 band — still concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members. Growth flattens in GovProgramCo categories where auto-approval removed the winnable targets; bot vendors pivot marketing toward members of non-signatory, non-transparent plans, where denial rates continued drifting up unopposed.

State statutes (W2): one additional state passes an AI-UR disclosure bill (running total within the 4-8 band for the game); operationalization lag of 3-7 years means zero in-game effect. The Vendor's comment letters appear in the record; so does the cynicism coverage of its side-switch.

Labor market: the denials-specialist shortage persists, but demand bifurcates — signatory books need exception managers and audit analysts (redeployment continues per doctrine), while long-tail hospitals bid up scarce appeals staff against rising unfenced denial drift. The Vendor sale transfers, rather than resolves, the appeals-talent concentration.

Non-player employers (W2 1-in-4: hit): one external jumbo signs Model Terms v1.1-equivalent language — notably via RegionalMutual's standard offer rather than its own initiative; consultant channels carry the Green pre-registered results as asks, not adoptions, everywhere else. Background drift continues on all unfenced books: denials up roughly 0.2pp/yr, overturn rates sagging, per the evidence brief.
