Whether Summit's holstered IRE dossier and the calibration protocol's implicit concession ever surface in a post-game audit or qui tam context — the file exists on both sides.

resolutions.move: Meridian Evidence-Complete Claim: pre-pay defense extension
resolutions.rationale: Platform extension on a live production system fits the 12-24 month friction window (3.2); NationalCo's simultaneous annex signing converted the axis from symmetric cancellation to cooperative de-escalation (3.5), so findings rates and held-claim aging improve within bounded movement; the accepted 2-3 quarter rotation lag is recorded but NationalCo rotated less, not more, post-detente.

resolutions.move: Lakeview Compact Annex B: audit-in-lieu and pre-pay proportionality, bought with 2032 renewal
resolutions.rationale: Counterparty incentive was demonstrated in T2 (RegionalMutual monetizes Compact architecture commercially); mid-term amendment route has Annex A precedent; all terms checklist-clean process language. Largest single reduction in Lakeview adverse-action cost share available; 2032 dependency risk recorded as a standing exposure, not a scored event.

resolutions.move: Prairie utility completion and external subscription tier
resolutions.rationale: Own-book objective met: Prairie cost-to-collect moves from ~3% small-provider baseline toward benchmark within the ±35% cost-per-touch bound. External uptake lands single-digit exactly as gold-card/standards base rates predict (~3% analog); move was sized to pay at that scale, so thin diffusion is priced, not a failure. Vendor long-tail competition split an already-small market.

resolutions.move: Summit two-track: gold-card breadth negotiation with dossier held in reserve
resolutions.rationale: GovProgramCo's calibration protocol pre-empted the dossier — high-overturn categories auto-approved before the threat was played, delivering the relief but voiding the leverage. Gold-card threshold redesign entered a 2029 program cycle; base rate says meaningful breadth arrives 2031-2033 (+2-4 yr rule), so only redesign-initiation credit lands in-window. Green second-wave book performs per pre-registered data.

resolutions.move: NationalCo: accept v1.1, launch Prepay Accuracy Assurance Rider, sign Blue transparency annex
resolutions.rationale: Retention objective achieved — Tranche B held on Red paper, procurement black mark cleared; fee base converted from clawback-exposed contingency to clawback-proof fixed prepay fees per the payer-economics brief's ASO fee logic. Cost: permanent per-disputed-dollar compression and book-wide audit visibility into legacy billing, both recorded on the PI-yield line.

resolutions.move: RegionalMutual: network-wide Compact extension, flat-fee PI default, jumbo catch-basin bidding
resolutions.rationale: Dominant strategy for a slow stack per 3.5 — detente cuts its own admin cost while the Tranche A proof asset wins accounts in motion; the catch-basin held the retention index whole and landed one external jumbo. Margin drag on the small-provider tail and SLA-interest leakage at scale are recorded as real, small costs of the moat.

resolutions.move: GovProgramCo: UM Calibration Protocol plus ePA scale-up beyond attestation
resolutions.rationale: The flammable IRE line was extinguished by auto-approving categories Red was paying admin cost to lose slowly (appeal-overturn asymmetry per evidence brief §2); small Medicaid/MA MLR give-back accepted; timing rides the 2029 Stars measure sunset per the payer brief. ePA economics ($3.50 manual vs $0.05 electronic) make the retained discipline nearly free.

resolutions.move: NationalCo-led Algorithmic UM Governance Attestations (three independent filings)
resolutions.rationale: Cheap, achieved its stated aims: a fiduciary-defensibility artifact employer counsel actually filed, and a cap on forward damages theories. W2 rendered its litigation value untestable — Lokken settled cash-only without process terms regardless — and the legacy tail was never reachable. The sworn-benchmark exposure is a standing fact for any post-game world.

resolutions.move: Tranche B awards and the NationalCo endgame
resolutions.rationale: The engineered terminal-extension expiry forced the choice; NationalCo executed rather than bleed, so Green got full terms with minimal transition friction — better on the member-friction metric than the move itself budgeted. Both branches of the fork served Green's metrics, as designed.

resolutions.move: Model Terms v2: pre-pay PI schedule
resolutions.rationale: Signed onto Tranche B awards and RegionalMutual paper immediately, but 1-3 year renewal cycles mean coverage is a minority-to-partial share of the coalition book at end-2030; scored partially mature per milestone doctrine 4(C), exactly as Green's own move sheet anticipated. The arbitrage is closed on covered paper only.

resolutions.move: Fee-refund structured settlement via the Fee Menu Rider rail
resolutions.rationale: Undisputed arithmetic plus an existing contractual vehicle plus a visibly retained litigation alternative equals settlement inside 9 months — a realized, documented recovery before game end, which beats any pending complaint on every Green metric. Precedent that fee-credit riders cap carrier downside is recorded as the accepted price.

resolutions.move: Second-wave direct contracts live, results published, warranted-fee procurement standard adopted
resolutions.rationale: 1/1/2029 go-live per executed T2 term sheets; pre-registered publication travels the consultant channel — the only diffusion channel W2 has ever validated. Warranted-fee economics become the buyer-side default without any carrier's consent. Jumbo-only breadth cap stands per the T1 ledger; coalition-average spend effect stays small.

resolutions.move: Project Cleave: trustee-run breakup and sale of the appeals arm
resolutions.rationale: Adjudicated skeptically per doctrine: the separation is real (trustee, no earn-out, audited data destruction), and a 12-month dual-track sale closes — but at a forced-timeline discount, with buyers pricing the discoverable COI history and the utility-capped signatory TAM. Green staged re-qualification of the PI arm lands late-window, post-closing, dual-sourced.

resolutions.move: Warranted-SaaS as ASO market default
resolutions.rationale: RegionalMutual signs — it genuinely cannot build flat-fee PI delivery on a slow stack in 24 months — but NationalCo's own services arm undercuts the pitch exactly as Red's move sheet built it to, and the Green direct channel opens only after re-qualification, late and dual-sourced. ARR quality improves (subscription mix); absolute growth is modest.

resolutions.move: Pre-pay battleground land grab on both sides
resolutions.rationale: GovProgramCo and RegionalMutual module sales are real (both need defensible pre-pay process), but Annex B audit-in-lieu and evidence-complete submission shrank pre-pay disputed volume on signatory books just as the products shipped — the pool moved again. Long-tail provider deployment runs 12-24 months, so most of that thesis is sold as pipeline. Pre-separation dual-selling in the same category is ledgered as one final COI exhibit.

resolutions.move: Lobbying reversal to transparency-mandate advocacy
resolutions.rationale: W2 statute physics are unforgiving: 4-8 state passages over the whole game, 3-7 year enactment-to-operationalization lag. One state disclosure bill passes in-window; nothing operationalizes by 2030. Milestone credit and exit-narrative repositioning only — precisely the outcome the Vendor's own assumptions priced.

turns.bluePosture: Consolidate and extend — Blue does not open a new front this turn; it moves the existing fight upstream. T2 proved the pattern: cooperative architecture with RegionalMutual pays rent, symmetric escalation with NationalCo cancels on headlines and inflates admin cost. NationalCo's pivot into pre-pay itemized-bill review and DRG validation is the one axis where our appeals automation cannot reach, so the T3 objective is to make pre-pay review economically sterile rather than to out-fight it: evidence-complete claims at submission, proportionality criteria that convert clean history into pre-pay exemption, and utility scale that drops cost-per-touch for the small archetypes. Every instrument is a process term (gold-card criteria, audit-in-lieu, SLAs, data standards) drafted to pass the signability checklist, and the Green RFP import channel — the only diffusion accelerant White has ever credited — is deliberately fed. Win condition math: leakage decline is driven by initial-denial prevention (not overturn volume), adverse-action cost share falls via utility scale and pre-pay cycle collapse, and margins hold for at least Meridian, Prairie, and Summit even if Lakeview only holds flat.
blueMoves: Evidence-Complete Claim: extend the production stack into pre-pay defense
Compact Annex B: prepayment proportionality and audit-in-lieu, bought with early renewal
Utility at scale: complete the Vendor exit and open external subscription
Summit two-track: gold-card breadth with GovProgramCo, dossier held in reserve
turns.redPosture: Selective detente, monetized. Turn 3 is Red's harvest-and-hold turn: lock the employer book down with signable transparency paper (which RegionalMutual has already proven survivable and which now costs less than losing accounts), convert PI economics from clawback-exposed contingency recoveries to clawback-proof fixed-fee prepay-accuracy revenue, and ride the 2029 Stars measure sunset while pre-emptively defusing the IRE overturn line item White flagged as flammable. On fully-insured books we deliberately moderate denial aggression (MLR rebate leakage makes marginal denials near-worthless there); on ASO we defend fee revenue by changing its form, not its volume. Intra-coalition competition is a feature: any employer book in motion must land on a Red carrier, never on Green direct contracting or an outside carrier, because the retention index scores exits, not shuffles.
redMoves: Capitulate on paper, convert the fee base
Scale the detente into a moat
Defuse the flammable line, keep the sunset gains
Governance hardening ahead of the Lokken window
greenMoves: Tranche B awards and the NationalCo endgame
Model Terms v2: extend the architecture to pre-pay payment integrity
Cash the fee-refund exposure via structured settlement, not litigation
Second-wave direct contracts go live; publish pre-registered results
vendorMoves: Project Cleave: binding breakup and dual-track exit of the appeals-automation arm
Warranted-SaaS as the ASO market default at the 2029-2030 renewal wall
Pre-pay battleground land grab: products where the disputed dollars actually moved
Lobbying reversal: from corridor-killer to transparency-mandate profiteer

cellAssessments.blue: Ranked second; win conditions substantially met. The negotiated-defense-plus-asymmetric-build posture was validated: leakage and adverse-action cost both improving moderately by end-game, three of four member margins improving. Its best decisions were economic targeting (the never-resubmitted 40% of denials required no counterparty consent), pricing the Compact with renewal terms RegionalMutual actually wanted, building the shared utility so Prairie and Summit never attempted heroic self-builds, and engineering every data artifact for second use in Green's award evaluations. Its structural weakness: Blue never controlled its own diffusion — the architecture spread only on RegionalMutual's standard paper and Green's RFPs — and Summit's dossier-in-reserve play was neutralized before it could be spent.
cellAssessments.red: Ranked third, but this understates the quality of the controlled retreat. Retention held (account movement stayed carrier-to-carrier inside the coalition), Stars exposure ended low, and PI yield was conceded deliberately by converting fee form (contingency to warranted/flat/prepay-accuracy) before Green's clawback finished repricing it. RegionalMutual played the single best hand at the table — its T2 defection was simultaneously the coalition's best defense and the event that made Green's terms the market ask, and it monetized detente into a moat. NationalCo paid measurably for two turns of refusal before capitulating on identical terms. GovProgramCo's clock-reading (Stars measure sunset, calibration protocol) was skillful but leaves a discoverable implicit concession. Red was never cost-exhausted; every concession traced to the employer flank or litigation surface.
cellAssessments.green: Ranked first, and earned it. Green converted purchasing power into the game's only working diffusion channel and the first — effectively only — binding constraint on payer payment-integrity behavior. It banked everything collectible in-window: Tranche A/B awards on its paper, fee refunds settled through the carrier's own fee-credit rider (avoiding litigation while keeping the fiduciary file clean), direct contracts live with published pre-registered results, fiduciary exposure low throughout. Its discipline was the differentiator: carrier-neutral enforcement, rewarding the defector with real book, keeping every demand signable, and letting NationalCo's own disclosed fee menu anchor the market against it.
cellAssessments.vendor: Ranked fourth; the dual-side arms-merchant thesis is dead on this record. T1 delivered real ARR growth but left written COI disclosures on White's ledger that compounded into a valuation discount every subsequent turn: Green disqualification, compressed take-rates extracted by NationalCo citing the Vendor's own file, a narrowed compliance-engine ruling on data-provenance grounds. The patient-bot stake taken mid-requalification was the decisive unforced error. The treaty-capture play found zero buyers because no corridor ever existed to kill and no signatory would hire a conflicted certifier. The endgame — real breakup, forced-timeline sale, clean-half re-qualification — was coherent salvage, and its one durable contribution (warranted-fee economics) was expropriated as everyone's standard.

criticalJunctures: T1: Blue's Clean Adjudication Compact and RegionalMutual's Edit Transparency Compact turn out to be the same instrument priced differently and merge into one signed bilateral, paid with 2027 renewal terms — the seed crystal for everything that diffused later.

T2 hinge: RegionalMutual breaks ranks and accepts Green's Model Terms substantially intact, taking Tranche A. The defection is simultaneously Red's best defensive play and Green's proof the RFP threat was real; it converts Green's paper into the market ask.
T2: NationalCo answers Blue's appeals automation by migrating recovery volume into pre-pay itemized-bill review and DRG validation — moving the war upstream and setting the T3 battleground.

T2: The Vendor takes a patient appeal-bot minority stake in the same nine months it petitions Green for COI re-qualification — the unforced error that hands Green a fresh exhibit, kills re-qualification, and forces the exit-engineering pivot.

T3: NationalCo's double capitulation at terminal-extension expiry — executing Model Terms v1.1 and signing the twice-refused edit-transparency annex, shorn of the steerage condition — after two turns of symmetric escalation made opacity a cost center.
T3: RegionalMutual extends Compact terms network-wide as a standard renewal rider — the single act that pushes the architecture past the table to non-signatory providers and one external jumbo.

T3: GovProgramCo publishes the UM Calibration Protocol, auto-approving what the IRE was overturning anyway — defusing the board's most flammable line item and disarming Summit's held-in-reserve dossier before it could be played.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By end-2030 the payer-provider claims war in this excursion has not been won, lost, or regulated away — it has been contractualized. The operative order is a lattice of bilateral, renewal-gated process instruments: machine-readable edit-library disclosure, 75-day change notice, mutual audit protocols with cure periods and interest, published gold-card entry/exit criteria extended from prior authorization into claims review, pre-pay proportionality and audit-in-lieu terms, and fee structures converted from contingency-on-recovery to warranted flat fees with overturn-linked rebates. No party ever signed, or even proposed, a numeric denial-rate commitment; the peace is made entirely of procedure and pricing, never of outcomes. The enforcement mechanism is not government — CMS stayed attestation-and-forbearance throughout, courts settled everything confidential and cash-only with no precedent, and state statutes will not operationalize until years after the horizon. The enforcer is the employer-purchaser: ERISA fiduciary leverage, RFP awards, fee clawbacks, and audit rights made transparency the price of keeping the ASO book. Adverse-action activity migrated upstream (denials to pre-pay itemized-bill/DRG review) when the denial channel was contested, then shrank on disclosed books as evidence-complete submission and proportionality terms sterilized the new battleground. Critically, the peace is partial and bordered: it covers the table's signatory books and one payer's network via a standard renewal rider, while the non-signatory long tail continues to experience unfenced denial drift (~0.2pp/yr) with sagging overturn rates — a widening disclosed-versus-opaque divide that is the most likely ignition source for the next escalation cycle. The conflict-services vendor layer was forced to demerge and exit rather than toll the peace; its one durable invention, warranted-fee economics, was absorbed as everyone's standard. Nothing external rescued anyone: every maturity was purchased at the table, on contract clocks.
rapporteur.excursionSummary: Game B2G2 ran doctrine D1 (negotiated posture) in world W2 (slow, forbearing environment) and produced a negotiated administrative peace enforced by purchasers rather than regulators. Turn 1 was a positioning turn: the one real event was the merger of Blue's and RegionalMutual's convergent transparency compacts into a single signed bilateral, priced with 2027 renewal commitments, while NationalCo scaled ASO payment integrity as a fee-revenue engine, Green put model terms with a PI-fee clawback into the RFP cycle, and the Vendor booked ARR while leaving conflict-of-interest paper on the ledger. Turn 2 was the hinge: RegionalMutual broke ranks and accepted Green's clawback terms to take Tranche A of the coalition book — a defection that was simultaneously Red's best retention defense and the event that converted Green's paper into the market ask. Meridian's two-year appeals/pre-adjudication build reached production and attacked the historically unfought 40% of denials; NationalCo rationally migrated recovery volume upstream into pre-pay itemized-bill and DRG review, producing the classic symmetric-escalation result on that axis — canceling headlines, inflating both admin ledgers. Green's fiduciary audits confirmed contingency fees booked on later-reversed recoveries and opened refund demands through NationalCo's own fee-credit rider. Turn 3 closed the loop: NationalCo capitulated at terminal-extension expiry (accepting the employer terms and the twice-refused edit-transparency annex) after opacity became a cost center; RegionalMutual extended Compact terms network-wide as its standard renewal rider — the only diffusion beyond the table; Annex B and evidence-complete claims sterilized the pre-pay battleground on disclosed books; GovProgramCo's calibration protocol defused its IRE-overturn exposure and disarmed Summit's dossier; and the Vendor, compounding COI discounts each turn, executed a real breakup and a discounted exit. Final ordinal ranks: Green first, Blue second, Red third, Vendor fourth. Analytically, three mechanisms did the work. First, the employer channel was the game's only binding constraint on payer behavior and only diffusion accelerant — regulation stayed symbolic, courts settled without process terms, statutes lagged past the horizon. Second, every instrument that bound was a process or fee term; numeric denial-rate commitments were never proposed by anyone. Third, everything ran on contract and deployment clocks: 12-24 month builds, 1-3 year renewal gates, diffusion reaching only 'early external adopters' by 2030. The peace is real but bordered — non-signatory books drifted worse all game, and that disclosed-versus-opaque gap is the residual instability the end-state carries forward.
keyDynamics: Employer purchasing power, not regulation, was the binding constraint: Green's RFP awards, clawback terms, and CAA fiduciary audit rights moved payer behavior while CMS forbore, courts settled without terms, and statutes lagged beyond the horizon.

Asymmetric capability build beat symmetric escalation: Blue's cooperative architecture with RegionalMutual paid measurable rent, while the Blue-NationalCo adversarial axis produced canceling headline metrics and mutual admin-cost inflation until NationalCo capitulated.

Adverse-action volume migrated upstream under pressure — from post-pay denial recovery into pre-pay itemized-bill/DRG review — and only shrank when prevention (evidence-complete claims) and proportionality terms (Annex B) made the new channel economically sterile on disclosed books.

Fee-structure innovation diffused faster than any process instrument: warranted-fee economics (fixed fee plus overturn-linked rebate) became the convergent standard across all sellers within two turns because every seller independently profited from offering it, while process terms crawled on renewal gates.

Intra-coalition defection drove the peace: RegionalMutual's rank-break was the hinge event, and Red's internal competition (any book in motion must land on a Red carrier) did more to spread the architecture than Blue's advocacy.

Documented conflicts of interest compounded as a valuation discount: the Vendor's T1 COI paper trail was cited by Green (disqualification), NationalCo (take-rate cuts), and buyers (exit multiple), killing the dual-side model without any regulator acting.

Everything matured on contract and deployment clocks — 12-24 month builds, 1-3 year renewal cycles, 5-7 year diffusion base rates — so end-game standings were determined by what was planted in Turn 1 and paid for at the table; no external shock rescued or punished anyone.

registryScores.evidence: The displacement mechanism fired exactly as predicted in channel terms: when Meridian's T2 appeals automation contested the denial channel (including the unfought 40%), NationalCo migrated recovery volume into pre-pay itemized-bill review and DRG validation 'where appeals automation cannot yet reach' — a non-denial adverse-action channel — within the same turn. However, White's ledger in this game reports state directionally, not as a dollar-by-channel adjudication ledger, so the displacement ratio (>=0.33) cannot be computed, and a single D1xW2 game cannot test invariance. Also noted: by T3 the displaced pool shrank on disclosed books once Annex B/evidence-complete claims sterilized pre-pay — displacement occurred but was not indefinitely conserved. Qualitative support for the channel-shift core; quantitative and invariance components untestable here.

The W2 channel-shift rider is supported for Red/Vendor artifacts: every boomerang ran through negotiation/procurement/employer channels, never regulators. NationalCo's disclosed Fee Menu Rider became 'the market pricing anchor cited in every fee negotiation at the table, including against NationalCo'; its fee-credit rider became the settlement vehicle for Green's refund demands; its documented annex refusals sat in Green's procurement file; the Vendor's COI disclosures were weaponized by Green (disqualification, twice) and NationalCo (take-rate cuts). Lag and channel match the W2 prediction. But the universal claim ('in no world do >=50% of published artifacts remain cost-free') is contradicted within this game: Blue's published artifacts (open model terms, transparency reports, published direct-contract results) and GovProgramCo's charters were net-positive with zero adverse citation in-window; the T3 attestations carry only latent exposure. Boomerang was publisher-selective, not universal.

No per-turn Blue cost ledger with cost-per-denial dollars appears in this game's White record; state variables are directional bands only. The qualitative toll structure is visible — recurring audit cycles, attestation filings, utility subscription fees, governance hardening, Annex SLA administration all persist through T3 even as escalation falls to 'low' — but neither the $65/$80 floor nor the volume-down/cost-up correlation can be computed from this record. No verdict on the ratio pattern is honest.

Every Red de-escalation in this game codes to external triggers, none to cumulative cost pain. ASO PI was explicitly fee-revenue-positive (T1: ~20 cents near-pure-margin fee income per recovered ASO dollar, no MLR drag), and Red's PI yield decline was 'deliberately conceded' fee compression 'it partly chose.' Proximate triggers: RegionalMutual's detente/defection — employer channel (Green awards, retention index); NationalCo's T3 capitulation — employer terminal-extension leverage plus escalation-induced opacity costs, executed at RFP expiry; discovery hygiene and governance attestations — litigation pricing (Lokken clock); GovProgramCo's moderation — regulatory measure timing (Stars). White's T3 adjudication states no external rescue occurred and Red 'held' rather than exhausted. Caveat: this is D1xW2, not the D2 stress cell, and the ASO P&L split was not published as a formal ledger — but the trigger-coding test is cleanly met.

The corridor half is strongly supported: across three turns and ~30 ruled instruments, zero numeric denial-rate corridors were signed, proposed, or even attempted — the Vendor's corridor-kill lobbying 'found no buyers' because 'no one proposed corridors to kill,' and White noted 'no denial-rate number appears anywhere' repeatedly. Every signed instrument was a process/fee/disclosure/audit term from the signable set. The doctrine-artifact half (detente rates under D2/D3 below one third) is untestable: this is a single D1 game, which can only confirm that D1 produces negotiated convergence — consistent with, but incapable of testing, the claim that the convergence is doctrine physics rather than strategy.

The discriminating test requires paired publisher vs internal-governor adverse-event rates (SIU audit, qui tam, acuity-accusation counts), and no such adverse events materialized against any charter publisher in-window: the three T3 Algorithmic UM Governance Attestations were 'never tested in court,' GovProgramCo's published charters drew no audit action under W2 forbearance. The single-game data point trends mildly against the hypothesis — publications functioned net-positive as contract exhibits and fiduciary artifacts — but the exposure the hypothesis predicts is explicitly ledgered as latent (attestations as future 'high-grade adverse fact,' the calibration protocol's implicit miscalibration concession, Summit's dossier surviving into post-game qui tam space) and the W2 litigation clock ran out before it could bite. Cannot be scored on this record.

Zero distress events occurred in any tier: no distress sale, no exclusive-terms delegation capture, no PE acquisition anywhere in the three-turn record. Prairie (rural-small) survived via the coalition utility on economics, not scoring protection; Lakeview merely 'holds flat'; the Vendor's appeals arm was the only distressed sale in the game and it is not a provider. A D1xW2 game where Blue's negotiated posture succeeded is the least stressful cell for this hypothesis; the absence of mid-tier distress here is a weak datum toward the seed-specificity worry but cannot carry a verdict without the D3 and protection-removed contrast cells.

The two testable components are supported. Timing: binding wins distributed across the whole horizon on renewal gates — Compact binding at 2027 renewals, Annex A/Tranche A on 2028 paper, Annex B/v1.1-at-NationalCo/Tranche B/network rider landing 2029-2030, with coalition coverage explicitly 'renewal-by-renewal' and majority-but-incomplete at end-2030; no single year visibly holds a dominant share and nothing resembling a synchronized 2028 window appears. Wedge-first: the first-cycle instrument (the Compact) was pure process terms — edit disclosure, notice, audit, gold-card criteria — with fee economics (clawback, warranted fees, prepay riders) arriving only in later cycles on separate paper. The third component (D2 escalation peaking 2029-30) is untestable in this D1 game, where escalation peaked mid-game at 'moderate' and fell to 'low' by end — consistent with D1 expectations but silent on the D2 claim.

The hypothesis turns entirely on D2xW2/W3 frequencies, and this is a D1 game. As control-arm data it contributes one consistent point: under D1 with a slow world, the game did not end in grinding uncoordinated escalation — the one symmetric-escalation axis (Meridian vs NationalCo) was resolved by negotiated capitulation, and end-state escalation was 'low.' That is compatible with the <=15% D1 baseline the confirm criteria assume, but the decisive D2 cells are absent.

Single-cell data, consistent with the table where testable. Robust strategies observed non-negative: renewal loading (Compact and Annex B both purchased with renewal terms, both paid), prevention-over-appeals (evidence-complete claims and pre-adjudication drove the moderate leakage improvement; White credited initial-denial prevention, not overturn volume), BATNA-first (Green's direct-contract term sheets were 'a rules-recognized threat to the retention index even before a member moves' and priced every negotiation). Fragile strategies observed negative: symmetric escalation canceled on headlines and inflated both admin ledgers until NationalCo abandoned it; weaponized-transparency-as-offense (Vendor's treaty capture, Summit's dossier) yielded zero leverage credit. Not testable: the 40-posture-point attribution threshold, governance-seat occupation and upcoding inoculation payoffs, the 7-of-9-cell tabulation, and the D2 escalation-first sign-flip.

In this GREEN-active W2 game the first — and effectively only — binding constraint on Red PI behavior on self-funded volume originated in the employer channel: Green's clawback/award structure forced RegionalMutual's T2 rank-break, flattened NationalCo's PI yield 'under fee compression it partly chose,' and drove the T3 conversion of the entire fee base to clawback-proof warranted structures. The statutory channel produced literally nothing in-window (regulatoryPressure 'low' all three turns; statutes 3-7 years from operationalization; CMS attestation-only; one AG inquiry closed without action). Contagion also ran through the purchasing channel: Compact-equivalence terms reached NationalCo and one external jumbo via RFP paper and carrier standard-forms while zero adopters arrived via statute. Caveats: no GREEN-inactive control run exists in this game, and this is D1 rather than the designated D2 comparison cell — but the channel-coding test is unambiguous on this record.

Arms-dealer intent and conduct are documented — private posture to 'kill or capture anything that actually reduces dispute volume,' corridor-kill lobbying, contingency appeals contracts to the sub-scale half of Blue, a talent raid that materially cost GovProgramCo its 0057-F schedule cushion and inflated payer-side wages. But the extension effect was largely neutralized rather than realized: treaty capture found no buyers, the COI screens (Green's standard, White's ledger) blocked the certifier and long-tail plays, Prairie exited to the coalition utility, and by T2-T3 the Vendor was monetizing the detente instead of the conflict, ultimately exiting. The formal test is incomplete: no VENDOR-inactive control run of the same seeds exists, and the scripted payer-acquisition side-switch inject never fired (the appeals arm sold late-window to an unnamed buyer; data-rights protections were papered by the T2 conversion ruling but never stress-tested). Verdict: incentive mechanism confirmed, conflict-extension effect contained, inject premise untested.

This is a W2 game with no preemption seed; no federal action of any kind occurred (CMS forbearance throughout, one symbolic RFI). Incidentally consistent with the hypothesis's background logic: the state/federal regulatory rail carried zero load in this game — all binding constraints coded to contract terms, litigation pricing, and the employer channel even without preemption — but the shock itself and its W3 comparison cells are absent.

No acquisition-enabled/disabled contrast exists in this record and no Red acquisition move was priced, proposed, or adjudicated. The one observable datum cuts toward the refute branch: when its denial channel was constrained, Red's revealed response sequence was migrate-upstream (pre-pay review), then negotiate process terms and convert fee structures — never acquire provider assets — and no integration-bypass end-state emerged. Classic VBC likewise stayed absent (direct contracts here are jumbo-only sponsor-provider deals, breadth 'permanently capped'). But absent evidence that acquisition was enabled and priced in this cell, Red's non-acquisition cannot be scored as a preference test.

In this cell the floor is cleared many times over: at least four distinct bilateral process-term instruments from the payer-signable set were signed and sustained to end-game — the Compact plus Annexes A/B (edit-library disclosure, 75-day notice, mutual audit, gold-card criteria, PI-vendor rider), the NationalCo edit-transparency annex, the RegionalMutual network-wide extension rider, and GovProgramCo's published gold-card/calibration programs — with two of three Red archetypes operating the architecture by 2030 and the T3 signability gate passing every instrument unmodified. As a single-cell test of a nine-cell universal claim this confirms only D1xW2, the friendliest corner; the decisive D2xW3/D3xW3 corners remain untested. But this game is an unambiguous pass for its cell, and the constructive claim — payers will sign process terms even while refusing all outcome terms — is the single most consistently reproduced fact in the record.

surprises: The peace was carried by intra-Red competition, not Blue or Green pressure per se: RegionalMutual's defection was simultaneously the coalition's best defensive play and the diffusion event — the architecture spread because a payer found detente profitable to sell, not because providers or employers forced it door-to-door.

A fee-structure class (warranted flat fee plus overturn-linked rebate) diffused faster than any process instrument in the game, including to non-player payers — instrument classes spread when every seller independently profits from offering them, while process terms crawl on renewal gates. Diffusion speed is a property of seller incentives, not of instrument merit.

The Vendor's fatal wounds were entirely self-inflicted paperwork: written COI disclosures and a mistimed patient-bot stake did more damage than any opposing move, compounding as a valuation discount no regulator ever touched. White's ledger of discoverable facts functioned as the game's real enforcement mechanism.

GovProgramCo's calibration protocol converted the board's most flammable exposure (IRE overturn drift) into a defensive asset while simultaneously disarming Summit's held-in-reserve dossier — giving Summit the relief and denying it the leverage credit. Preemptive self-correction outplayed adversarial evidence-holding.

The formal accountability institutions produced zero architecture: Lokken and all copycats settled confidential with no process terms, CMS never enforced, the AG inquiry closed in one turn. Litigation's entire contribution was behavioral caution during the discovery window — the shadow of the law worked; the law itself never arrived.

By Turn 3 the signability gate passed every instrument unmodified for the first time — the table collectively learned to draft from the ruled corpus, suggesting that in slow worlds the binding constraint on cooperation is drafting knowledge, and it depletes fast once precedent accumulates.

The detente's border is its own instability: patient appeal-bots pivoted marketing to non-signatory opaque plans where denial drift ran unfenced all game, meaning the peace mechanically concentrated the remaining conflict on the books least equipped to fight it.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High fidelity to W2 in substance, with one structural deviation. Faithful elements: statutes stay within the 4-8 state band with 3-7yr operationalization lags and zero in-game bite; courts produce no precedent — Lokken and all copycats settle confidential, cash-only, with NO process terms, and the only behavioral effects are pre-settlement discovery hygiene, exactly per the litigation-clock rule; CMS remains attestation-driven and forbearing through game end with real teeth deferred beyond 2030 ('if any, arrive T7+' honored); media flares are single-cycle and decay as specified (T1 hit, T2 miss, T3 one hit); patient-AI lands at exactly the W2 ceiling of 8-10% by end-2030, concentrated in commercially insured high-literacy members; employers are inertial with audit-rights demands at the 1-in-4 rate (one in T2, one in T3); FTC/AGs are reactive-only (one inquiry, closed without action); no external forcing function rescues any strategy — the cross-world design note's W2 test ('no external forcing function') is respected in the final adjudication. Deviations: (1) the spec declares 1 turn = ~6 months with 8-10 turns, but the record runs three turns of 12-24 months, following the Common Rules' '18-month turn' language instead — per-turn event-frequency dice were only informally pro-rated (e.g., '1-in-4 across the 24-month window'), though aggregate event counts approximate what 8 six-month W2 turns would produce; (2) the spec says CMS 'grants 0057-F extensions' through T4-T5, whereas the record uses attestation-based discretion with 'no extension formally granted or needed' — functionally equivalent forbearance, cosmetically different.

The adjudicator consistently enforced renewal gating, the 12-24 month IT lag, pilot-scale strikes, and honest diffusion-stage scoring (Compact capped at early-external-adopters, infrastructure 2033+).

Down-weight the claim that warranted-fee (fixed-fee + overturn-rebate) PI economics become a cross-market standard by 2030 — external non-player payer adoption within ~2 years outruns every contract-diffusion base rate in the table; treat it as table-actor convergence only.
Down-weight the gold-card 'low double digits on targeted service lines' coverage figure toward the single-digit Texas anchor when extracting quantitative lessons about carve-out programs.

Treat per-turn W2 event-frequency conclusions cautiously: the game compressed 8-10 six-month turns into three 12-24 month turns, so frequency guidance was approximated in aggregate rather than diced per the spec.
The off-screen assumption that 4-8 state statute passages occurred (only 1-2 adjudicated on-screen) should not be cited as an adjudicated outcome.

games.name: Regulatory Theater
games.seed: Both sides open with legal/regulatory strategy as their PRIMARY theater: Blue pursues state AI-UR legislation, litigation support, and evidence dossiers; Red pursues safe-harbor lobbying, preemption advocacy, and voluntary-standard preemption plays. Operational AI deployment continues on both sides but as the secondary front. What the regulatory environment actually delivers is governed strictly by the active world-model.

turns.narrative: The loudest theater delivered the least. Both coalitions poured 2026-27 into the statute books, and the W2 environment absorbed the energy like wet sand. Blue's Overturn Dossier launched cleanly — after White forced it into an independently administered, de-identified registry structure — and generated one national news cycle before coverage moved on. Two or three states passed SB 1120-style bills, but with delayed effective dates and no enforcement appropriations; Red's Responsible AI Conformance Standard, converted to a legitimate open-SDO form, was shopped to the same legislatures as an off-ramp. White records the irony: Red will claim the safe harbor "blocked" bills that the base rate says were mostly dying in committee anyway. Neither side's regulatory offensive produced an adjudicable win, and both bought lobbying invoices that show up as admin cost — Vendor's Alliance collected fees from the entire drafting contest. The move that actually paid this turn was the one with no press release: NationalCo's pivot from prior-auth (publicly retired, loudly marketed) to pre-pay itemized-bill review and DRG validation on ASO volume. Fee revenue rose a moderate band; headline denial rates stayed flat because PA eliminations masked edit growth; and Blue's dossier, keyed to denial statistics, did not detect the substitution this turn. The countervailing force is already in writing, though: Green's Fiduciary Rider — with its fee caps and ban on fees for carrier-self-generated findings — is sitting in live 2027-28 RFPs, and its 408(b)(2) demands were served on both national carriers before a targeted suit was filed against NationalCo late in the turn. Under W2 court clocks, no ruling arrives before T2, and the J&J/Wells Fargo standing precedents make dismissal a live risk. Lakeview reached a partial rider at renewal — gold-carding, SLAs, notice terms — but RegionalMutual, offered early peace bundled with the Gold-Card Compact, refused the PI-fee clawback. Summit ran the turn's cleanest Blue play, harvesting existing gold-card programs for a real reduction in PA burden. GovProgramCo quietly conceded its worst post-acute denial tail and volunteered as CMS's 0057-F showcase — prudent, though CMS's signaled enforcement flexibility cheapened the showcase. Vendor sold to all four cells, though White struck its contingency-on-prevented-dollars pricing for medical-necessity UM modules as denial-based compensation, and logged three latent conflict facts — the Alliance funding trail, the Prairie/Summit training-data arrangement, and the auditor-participant position with Green — none surfaced yet, all discoverable. Everything decisive now waits on the 2027-28 renewal cohort.
env: CMS sub-regulatory signal (W2 CMS posture): FAQ guidance indicates 0057-F compliance will be assessed on attestation and 'good-faith implementation' for an initial period; trade press covers it, general media does not. Laggard payers quietly slow API spend; Vendor connector urgency softens late in the turn.

State legislative cycle (W2 statute rate): two to three states enact SB 1120-style human-in-the-loop bills with effective dates pushed 12-18 months out and no dedicated enforcement budgets; several more bills die in committee — a fate the base rate assigns regardless of Red's safe-harbor lobbying or Blue's dossier testimony.

Media flare (W2: 1-in-2, decays next turn): Blue's first quarterly Overturn Dossier lands a one-cycle national story on overturned denials; a same-week trade piece on provider documentation-AI 'coding optimization' keeps coverage roughly symmetric per W2. No sustained campaign develops; the story is dead by the following quarter.

Court docket (W2 clocks): Lokken discovery production continues under the pre-existing order — documents flow but no merits event; Kisting-Leung fiduciary claims proceed without ruling; Green's new suit and any ERISA-preemption test case cannot reach decision before T2. One AG office opens an informal inquiry into algorithmic denials and takes no further action (W2 reactive posture).

Patient-AI appeal tooling (W2 niche growth): assisted appeals rise from ~2% toward ~3-4% of adverse determinations, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members — incremental volume lands mostly on the medical-necessity denial categories, not the coding-validation edits Red is shifting toward.

Non-player employer behavior (W2 inertial): the renewal cohort overwhelmingly re-signs incumbent carriers; exactly one non-coalition jumbo account demands audit rights, citing the Overturn Dossier coverage, and accepts Red's ASO Transparency Rider as the answer.

The conflict-audit clause is satisfied by Vendor's Information-Barrier Attestation; White logs the tension between the charter's BAA data limits and Vendor's quiet use of small-archetype claims to train its premium tier as a latent discoverable fact.

No court reaches the ERISA preemption question this turn (3-5 yr merits clock). Discovery hygiene is real going forward but cannot reach pre-2026 documents already under the Lokken discovery order.

resolutions.rationale: Best base-rate-aligned move of the turn: pre-pay is already ~43% of a PI market growing 13-15% CAGR, automated review costs ~$0.05/transaction, and ASO recoveries are fee revenue with zero MLR drag. PI yield up a moderate band within rule 3.3 bounds; headline denial rates flat as PA eliminations offset edit growth. Second-order ledger records rising provider inpatient-claim friction and Green's rider language aimed squarely at this revenue at 2027-28 renewals.

resolutions.rationale: Connector contracts signed with RegionalMutual, GovProgramCo, and three Blue archetypes — 0057-F compulsion is the turn's one exogenous certainty — though CMS's signaled flexibility softened deadline urgency late in the turn. Talent raid lands roughly half its targets against NationalCo non-solicit friction. The Green audit wedge stalls: Green's own carve-out diligence exposed the auditor-participant conflict, and the coalition engages warily or not at all.

turns.bluePosture: Regulatory offense, operational patience. Blue's primary theater this turn is legal/evidentiary: convert the single strongest fact in the environment — 80.7% of appealed MA denials overturned in 2024 — into a coalition-wide evidence dossier that feeds state legislation, litigation discovery, and AG referrals, making opaque algorithmic UR legally and reputationally expensive before Red's safe-harbor lobbying can mature. turns.narrative: Turn 2 was decided at award tables, not in courtrooms — though the courtroom supplied the loudest noise. Green's RFP cycle did what statutes could not: both national-table carriers executed the Fiduciary Rider, clearing White's pre-stated two-carrier threshold. NationalCo signed while reshaping — contingency on self-generated findings replaced by a fixed PEPM program fee sized to recapture most of the old economics, plus a contingency tail on independently verified findings. Green counsel saw the recapture, lacked any gate basis to strike a fixed purchaser-vendor fee, and moved the fight to benchmarking in 2029, exactly as both sheets predicted. The demonstrative anchor jumbo left NationalCo anyway, fiduciary-committee minutes citing rider refusal — the turn's single media flare, one business-press cycle, dead within the quarter — and Red's retention index took its first scored dent. The standing motion broke against Red: sponsor-plaintiffs are not J&J participant-plaintiffs; plan-asset fee injury is concrete, and the court trimmed only the disclosure theory that NationalCo's voluntary 408(b)(2) production mooted. Prohibited-transaction and imprudence claims proceed, with discovery into PI fee schedules ordered and production due next turn. The association preemption suit was filed and briefed — the highest-variance object on the T3 docket. The quiet cooperative deal outperformed everything. RegionalMutual bought home-market peace: binding pre-claim adjudication on top DRG families, expanded gold-carding, line-level reason codes, clinician attestation on clinical-validation downgrades — in exchange for the clawback's death. Lakeview traded a compensation fight it could not survive for process terms that reprice edits at the source. Rule 3.5 paid both sides: home-market disputed volume fell and admin cost fell bilaterally; the only cell that lost by it was Vendor. Blue's registry v2 caught the substitution — partial-year data shows flat denials against rising pre-pay adjustments on ASO books — now feeding Green's forensic audit and the NationalCo discovery record. Prairie and Summit's utility, twelve months deployed, posted bounded cost-per-touch gains, and their conflict audit detonated the first latent Vendor fact, the training-data arrangement, on Blue's timing. Vendor absorbed it: Project Ledger's legal separation landed in-year, technical separation lags the IT window, the Green auditor engagement died under the independence charter — but EditGuard, early-locked Red renewals, and the patient-appeals acquisition kept ARR compounding. GovProgramCo executed its Stars-calendar arbitrage cleanly and dated every memo, paper White logs as discoverable. The W2 environment stayed molasses: attestation-based 0057-F, copycat bills dying in committee, an AG inquiry closed without action, patient-AI drifting to 4-5%.

turns.narrative: The final turn belonged to the quiet architecture. Meridian's first renewal window arrived exactly as both sheets predicted, and NationalCo — facing a 2029 production deadline, a benchmarking demand, and a rival payer's certainty paper already on Meridian's desk — chose normalization. The second dyad executed: full Lakeview-form process terms plus a certainty annex on top DRG families, with ASO applicability confined to coalition-sponsor accounts rather than network-wide. That signature cleared White's pre-stated diffusion threshold, and the rider class moved to piloted. RegionalMutual, having moved first, lost nothing by Meridian pressing coalition demands anyway; its Certainty Network converted the 2028 peace into a retention product with home-market sponsor signatures. Three payer-provider dyads now run binding pre-claim adjudication — the fastest-diffusing substantive instrument of the game, and the one no statute forced. The Green-NationalCo collision resolved as a merged settlement: bounded restitution, rider v3 executed coalition-wide, and — the concession Red swore it would not make — a market-check re-basing of the fixed PEPM against the discovery-derived benchmark, in exchange for three-year renewals that freeze the retention index through scoring. Both sides can honestly claim the deal; White records that Green priced the fee and Red held the book. NationalCo's rotation into COB, subrogation, FWA, and accuracy-as-a-service kept PI yield growing outside every cap at the table, while GovProgramCo's Stars-window recalibration landed inside bounds with a clean forward file — though the patient-AI milestone (assisted appeals reaching six to eight percent, concentrated on precisely those medical-necessity categories) pushed IRE volume up as the window closed. The W2 environment delivered its signature anticlimaxes: the association preemption suit died on ripeness without touching the merits; Lokken settled sealed, cash-only, no process terms; a single state levied a single-digit fine under a T1 statute; CMS attested its way to the horizon. Vendor cleaned house for exit — attestation completed, Alliance trail self-disclosed before anyone could detonate it, sponsor-direct stalling at three or four accounts, the clearing utility stripped of its binding pretensions and launched pilot-scale without an anchor payer. The exit clears, but on the split-sale track at an infrastructure-lite multiple: the dispute economy it was built to monetize is measurably smaller than the one it was bought into. Final ordinal posture: Blue reaches its moderate leakage decline with three of four archetypes improving; Red holds PMPM, yield, and a frozen retention index; Green converts architecture into priced spend relief with a closed prudence file; Vendor exits profitable but repriced. Cooperation, not escalation, moved every large number — exactly as Rule 3.5 said it would.
