rapporteur.excursionSummary:
Game B2G3 ran doctrine D1 in world W2 with GREEN and VENDOR cells active, seeded with legal/regulatory strategy as both coalitions' primary theater. The seed's premise self-liquidated within Turn 1: the W2 environment absorbed the entire statutory contest — bills passed without enforcement appropriations, Red's safe-harbor standard was converted to a voluntary SDO with no legal effect anywhere, the AG inquiry closed without action, and every consequential court event either settled sealed (Lokken), died on ripeness (Red's ERISA preemption suit), or delivered only procedural rulings. Across three turns, not one statute, precedent, or regulatory enforcement action ever bound any player's economics. "Regulatory Theater" proved literal: the theater consumed lobbying invoices and produced nothing adjudicable for either coalition.

The game's actual causal engine was purchaser power plus renewal-table contracting. Red executed the signature move in T1 — publicly retiring prior authorization while expanding pre-pay itemized-bill review and DRG validation on ASO volume — a substitution Blue's denial-keyed dossier missed for a full turn. Green, not Blue and not any regulator, imposed the first binding constraint on that fee engine: RFP awards conditioned on the Fiduciary Rider (two carriers executed at the T2 threshold), an anchor-jumbo defection, and a 408(b)(2) suit that survived standing and forced a pre-production settlement merging restitution, rider v3, and a discovery-benchmarked PEPM re-basing. Red conceded transparency and fee structure at every gate while never conceding the program itself, rotating yield into COB, subrogation, FWA, accuracy-as-a-service, and post-Stars-sunset MA channels that no instrument at the table measures.

The fastest-diffusing instrument was one the seed never contemplated: binding pre-claim adjudication certainty, pioneered by RegionalMutual's home-market peace and replicated at three dyads plus sponsor-facing riders — spreading because it made both signatories money. Cooperation, not escalation, moved every large number; the only structurally damaged cell was Vendor, whose dispute-pool-dependent book was repriced by the de-escalation it had quietly worked to prevent, forcing a split-sale exit at an infrastructure-lite multiple.

End-state: all three principal cells claim honest wins — Blue's moderate leakage decline, Red's held PMPM and frozen retention, Green's priced spend relief with a closed prudence file — while the underlying adverse-action contest continues in rotated, unmeasured channels. The coalition core operates on undiluted process-and-fee paper; the external market runs on Red's diluted conformed variant, diffused by incumbency and employer inertia, with settlement confidentiality having sealed the record that could have forced the undiluted version outward.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By 2030 the system settles into a privately ordered, contract-mediated equilibrium brokered by purchasers rather than regulators. The public regulatory apparatus is decorative: statutes exist but are unenforced (one symbolic single-digit fine), no algorithmic-denial merits precedent exists, preemption is unresolved for want of ripeness, and CMS holds an attestation posture through the horizon. Real governance lives in bilateral paper: two full payer-provider transparency/audit rider dyads, three binding pre-claim certainty compacts, and a coalition-wide fiduciary fee rider (v3) that caps and claws back payment-integrity fees on roughly 2M employer lives. Inside the coalition perimeter, disputed-dollar volume, admin cost, and PI fee extraction all measurably fell; escalation ended low. Outside the perimeter, the market runs on the incumbent carrier's diluted variant — disclosure without fee caps — and the adverse-action contest has not ended but rotated into channels no table instrument measures: COB, subrogation, FWA, accuracy-as-a-service, and MA utilization management recalibrated to the post-2029 Stars measure set. It is a two-tier peace: a governed core surrounded by an unmeasured frontier, with the measurement apparatus (Blue's registry, Green's audit tests) perpetually one channel behind the payer's rotation. Latent legal exposure (GovProgramCo's dated memos, rising patient-AI appeal volume on recalibrated MA categories) persists past the horizon without crystallizing. The AI arms race itself became economically secondary: the vendor arms dealer exited repriced, and the decisive weapons were procurement conditions, discovery deadlines, and renewal calendars, not models.
rapporteur.endStateName: The Purchaser's Peace (governed core, rotating frontier)
keyDynamics: Regulatory theater as heat sink: W2 absorbed both coalitions' primary-theater energy for three turns; no statute, precedent, or enforcement ever bound, and money moved only at renewal and award tables.

Substitution-and-rotation: Red repeatedly moved adverse-action yield one channel ahead of each new constraint (PA retreat to pre-pay edits/DRG validation; post-rider rotation to COB/subrogation/FWA/accuracy-as-a-service; MA UM recalibrated to the Stars measure sunset), keeping PI yield positive under every cap signed.

Employer channel as the only binding brake: Green's RFP conditioning, anchor-account defection, and sponsor-standing ERISA suit constrained Red's ASO fee engine where statutes and Blue's dossier could not.

Cooperative certainty as the diffusion winner: binding pre-claim adjudication spread to three dyads plus external adopters with zero statutory force, because it cut disputed volume and admin cost bilaterally (Rule 3.5 vindicated in the cooperative direction).

Measurement lag as strategic terrain: Blue's registry and Green's audit architecture were always one rotation behind Red's active channel; visibility, once achieved, moved money (PEPM re-basing, Meridian dyad) but never caught the current frontier.

Dilution-diffusion: the external ASO market adopted Red's conformed variant of Green's rider — disclosure architecture intact, compensation caps stripped — so the loser's redline, not the winner's template, became the modal market paper.

Conflict facts as traded munitions: Vendor's discoverable conflicts were detonated selectively (training-data fact), held as leverage (Alliance trail), or self-disclosed pre-emptively; none reached press, all reached pricing.
criticalJunctures: T1: Red's quiet rebalance — loud PA retirement masking pre-pay PI expansion on ASO — succeeds undetected because Blue's dossier was keyed to denial statistics; sets the substitution logic for the whole game.

T1: White's conversion rulings (registry to independent de-identified administrator; SDO to open form; UM contingency pricing struck) pre-hardened every published artifact and removed contingency compensation from the UM layer.

T2: Green's RFP awards clear the pre-stated two-carrier rider threshold and the anchor jumbo defects — the first scored dent in Red, achieved by procurement while both litigation tracks were still pending.
T2: Standing motion substantially denied on the sponsor-vs-participant distinction; PI-fee-schedule discovery ordered, creating the 2029 production deadline that priced the T3 settlement.
T2: RegionalMutual's home-market certainty peace — clawback dies in exchange for binding pre-claim adjudication — outperforms every adversarial move and becomes the game's replicated template.

T3: Pre-production settlement merges restitution, rider v3, PEPM re-basing, and a retention-freezing three-year renewal — and its confidentiality seals the benchmark record, capping external diffusion of the undiluted rider.
T3: Preemption suit dismissed on ripeness — the board's highest-variance object fizzles, confirming that private ordering, not federal doctrine, governs the 2030 end-state.

registryScores.evidence: Two clean displacement episodes in one game: (1) T1 PA retirement offset within the same turn by pre-pay itemized-bill review and DRG validation on ASO volume (fee revenue up a moderate band, headline denials flat — White adjudication explicit); (2) T3 rotation into COB/subrogation/FWA/accuracy-as-a-service after rider v3 capped the pre-pay edit channel, with PI yield still improving at game end. No numeric displacement ratio was ledgered in this record, so the 0.33 threshold is unverifiable, but the qualitative pattern — constrained channel value reappearing in adjacent non-denial channels within 1-2 turns — held both times a constraint bound. Single-cell (D1xW2) contribution only; invariance across cells untestable here.

In this W2 game, essentially no published artifact was weaponized against its publisher by end-game: Blue's registry/dossier (converted form) was net-positive and fed the PEPM re-basing and Meridian dyad; the joint certainty results publication was net-positive; Green's rider paper was net-positive; Red's SDO standard was inert but never adversely cited. The adverse-citation dynamic ran entirely through LATENT unpublished facts (Vendor's training-data arrangement detonated by Blue's conflict audit; Alliance trail held as leverage then self-disclosed). This exceeds the refute threshold (>=50% of published artifacts net-positive with no adverse citation) for this game. Major confound: every publication was White-converted into gated/independent-administrator form at T1, so the game may show that gated publication defuses the boomerang rather than that the boomerang is absent — one-game, one-cell contribution.

No per-turn Blue cost ledger or cost-per-denial figures appear anywhere in this game record; the discriminating computation cannot be run. Directional caution for the invariance claim: the certainty-architecture dyads produced BILATERAL admin-cost decline alongside falling disputed volume (T2-T3 adjudications), suggesting some tolls are avoidable through cooperative prevention rather than strictly recurring — worth checking against ledgered cells.

Every Red de-escalation in this game coded to external triggers, never cumulative cost: RegionalMutual's T2 home-market peace (employer/home-market retention value plus clawback avoidance), NationalCo's rider conformance (award-table retention after the anchor jumbo defection), and the T3 settlement (2029 discovery production deadline plus retention stapled to the release). Red PI activity on self-funded volume remained fee-revenue-positive throughout (redPIYield improving in all three turns); the T1 adjudication explicitly notes ASO PI is fee revenue, not savings, and Red's own sheet cites MLR floors as the reason to keep aggression on ASO. D1 game, so the D2-margin confirm criterion is out of scope, but the trigger-coding core of the hypothesis is cleanly supported here.

The signability half is strongly supported: across ~30 rulings in three turns, every signed instrument is process or compensation paper — reason codes, audit rights, notice/SLAs, gold-card criteria, clinician attestation, fee caps/clawbacks — and White repeatedly annotates 'no corridor anywhere in the text.' Zero numeric denial-rate corridors were signed, proposed, or even attempted; Blue's own T2 sheet says 'process terms only, no corridors.' The doctrine-frequency half (detente rate under D2/D3 below one third) is untestable in this D1 game; note the end-state here is a negotiated-instrument equilibrium under D1, consistent with but not probative of the doctrine-artifact claim.

No Blue actor published an AI-governance charter, and no SIU-audit, qui tam, or acuity-inflation adverse event was adjudicated against any actor in three turns, so the publisher-vs-internal-governor event-rate comparison has no data. Weak circumstantial consistency: the actor with the riskiest internal paper (GovProgramCo's dated Stars-sequencing memos) governed internally without publication and reached game end with exposure logged but uncrystallized — the 'govern internally, gate publication' posture was never punished here.

Zero distress events at any tier in this game: no distress sale, PE acquisition, or exclusivity-delegation capture of any Blue archetype, with scoring protection removed. The mid-tier archetypes ended improving (Lakeview locked a 3-year rider, Summit scaled direct contracting to a third tranche), and rural Prairie ended stronger than it started via the shared utility plus a free certainty seat. This is a one-cell (D1xW2) datum against the 'modal structural casualty' claim — it feeds the refute criterion's 'no mid-tier distress anywhere' arm but cannot settle it alone; the cooperative D1xW2 equilibrium may simply be the least distress-generating corner of the design.

Binding instruments distributed contract-by-contract across all four in-game years: Lakeview partial rider (2027), Lakeview full rider + RM certainty pilot + Green v2 awards (2028), Meridian dyad + rider v3 + Certainty Network (2029), settlement/renewal bundle (2030) — no single year visibly holds a dominant share, though the record gives counts, not dollar weights. First-cycle wins were unambiguously wedge provisions: T1 Lakeview got gold-carding/SLAs/notice only, with clawback and reporting deferred (and the clawback ultimately died); full economics (fee re-basing) arrived only in 2029-30 after two cycles of leverage accumulation. The D2 late-peak escalation sub-claim is out of scope; this D1 game's escalation index actually declined to low by T3.

This is a D1xW2 game; the hypothesis turns on F1 frequency in D2xW2/W3 versus a D1xW1 replication, none of which this game instantiates. For the record, the end-state here is not grinding uncoordinated escalation — escalation ended low and cooperative instruments dominated — which is consistent with a low D1 baseline but carries no weight on the D2 question.

One-cell evidence, and only for strategies actually played. Robust strategies committed to and paying non-negatively in D1xW2: renewal loading (both dyads, the game's core Blue engine), prevention-over-appeals (Summit clean-claim/gold-card harvest; certainty architecture), BATNA-first for the small tail (Prairie/Summit shared utility plus direct-contract exit threat — all positive). Governance-seat occupation and upcoding inoculation were not distinctly observable at the 40-point threshold. Fragile strategies were mostly avoided rather than tested: no corridor was ever attempted, Blue deliberately held the Vendor conflict fact as table leverage instead of press detonation, and neither side ran an appeal factory. Nothing here contradicts the table; little of it stress-tests it.

The cleanest hypothesis-to-record match in the game. First binding constraint on Red PI on self-funded volume was unambiguously the employer channel: T2 RFP awards conditioned on the Fiduciary Rider (two carriers executed), the anchor jumbo's departure, and the sponsor-standing 408(b)(2) suit — all before any statute was enforced anywhere (statutes stayed symbolic through the horizon; the lone state fine hit a non-player in 2030). Contagion also ran through purchaser/contract channels: gold-card and certainty terms reached three dyads plus external sponsor riders by 2029-30 while the statutory channel produced zero adopters. Caveats: no GREEN-inactive control was run against this seed, and the W1 contrast is out of scope — so the counterfactual arm of the confirm criteria is untested, but the core claim could not have performed better on this record.

Arms-dealer incentive behavior is directly documented: T1 lobbying explicitly aimed to 'keep disputed-dollar volume high' and steer bills away from dispute-shrinking structures; Vendor sold compliance to all four cells, then sold Blue (EditGuard) the countermeasure to the pre-pay weapon its own PI arm sharpened; White's T2 adjudication states symmetric escalation 'inflates both sides' admin spend, and Vendor books the difference,' and the T2 cooperative deal's only losing cell was Vendor. The dispute-pool dependence was confirmed in the negative at exit: de-escalation repriced the book to a split-sale at a discount. However, (a) no VENDOR-inactive control run exists for duration/term-adoption comparison, and (b) the scripted payer-acquisition-of-provider-side-vendor inject never fired (Vendor instead bought the patient-appeals tool), so the side-switch/data-rights half is untested.

No preemption seed fired in this W2 game, and Red's organic ERISA preemption vehicle was dismissed on ripeness without reaching merits — the shock condition never existed. Weak directional note: even with state statutes fully inert (functionally similar to a no-state-rail world), binding constraints migrated to private ordering, litigation pricing, and the employer channel exactly as H13 predicts for the post-shock environment, and no detente-via-regulation dynamic was ever observed to be crowded out.

Acquisition moves were not priced or enabled for Red in this D1xW2 cell (the designated cells were D2xW2 and D3xW3), and Red made no provider-asset acquisition attempt. Observed Red responses to binding constraints were channel rotation and negotiated process-term instruments — superficially aligned with the refute direction, but meaningless without an attractively priced acquisition option on the board. The only vertical move in the game was Vendor's patient-appeals acquisition, which is outside the hypothesis's scope.

The floor was cleared many times over in this cell: line-level edit reason codes and machine-readable disclosure, notice terms, bilateral audit rights, published rolling gold-card criteria, algorithmic-involvement disclosure, and clinician attestation all bound at renewals and were sustained to end-game (Lakeview 2027/2028 rider with 3-year lock; Meridian/NationalCo 2029 dyad; three certainty compacts), plus the coalition-wide Green rider v3. Every item on the payer-signable set appears in executed, sustained paper. This game also refines the mechanism: the process terms that spread fastest (pre-claim certainty) were the ones producing bilateral gains, not the ones extracted under duress. One cell only — the decisive D2xW3/D3xW3 corners remain untested.

cellAssessments.blue: Blue's decisive move was abandoning its own seed: after W2 swallowed the T1 statute campaign, Blue demoted the legal theater to a support function and won through measurement plus renewal contracting — Registry v2 caught Red's denial-to-edit substitution, two full rider dyads executed, certainty annexes locked, and the shared utility and direct-contract pilots produced bounded, scored results. Final position: moderate leakage decline, three of four archetypes improving. Blue's persistent weakness was lag — its instruments measured Red's previous channel each turn, never the current one (COB/subrogation and rotated MA lines end the game uncounted).
cellAssessments.red: Red played the most disciplined loss-minimization game at the table: substitution and rotation kept PI yield positive under every cap it signed, transparency was conceded everywhere economics could be preserved (fixed-PEPM recapture, diluted conformed variant winning the external market), and both litigation threats were neutralized by purchase (settlement with retention stapled) rather than verdict. The formal regulatory offensive — safe harbor, preemption — produced nothing. End state: PMPM held, retention frozen through scoring, fee engine intact but displaced into unmeasured channels, with GovProgramCo's discoverable Stars-arbitrage paper as the unpriced tail risk.
cellAssessments.green: Green was the game's effective protagonist and the only cell whose theory of the environment was correct from T1: ignore the statute contest, police plan-asset leakage through procurement and fiduciary law. RFP conditioning executed the rider at both national carriers, the sponsor-standing ruling converted litigation into a rider-diffusion and repricing engine, and the T3 benchmarking strike re-based the PEPM recapture. Costs of victory: settlement confidentiality sealed the record that would have diffused the undiluted rider externally, and rider architecture perpetually trails Red's channel rotation (v4 fight on bundled admin fees already visible).
cellAssessments.vendor: Vendor's arms-dealer thesis worked until cooperation broke it: three turns of selling weapons and countermeasures to every side compounded ARR, but the certainty architecture and Green's fee caps shrank the disputed-dollar pool the whole book monetized, and the conflict register (one fact detonated by Blue, one self-disclosed under deadline pressure) forced defensive separation spending. The pivot to neutral rails came one deployment cycle late; exit cleared on the split-sale fallback at a dispute-pool discount. Vendor is the game's clearest demonstration that the dispute economy, not either combatant, was the entity most damaged by peace.

surprises: The transparency boomerang never fired: zero published artifacts were adversely cited against their publishers in three turns — the weaponization dynamic ran entirely through latent unpublished facts (Vendor's conflict register), suggesting White's T1 conversion-gating of publications may be the operative protective mechanism.

The winner's template diffused in the loser's redline: Red's diluted 'Green-conformed' variant — Green's disclosure architecture with the compensation caps stripped — became the modal external ASO paper, meaning Green won the coalition and lost the market.

Litigation victory functioned as an anti-diffusion event: the settlement Green won sealed the discovery-derived benchmark record under confidentiality, cutting off exactly the public forcing function the undiluted rider needed to spread beyond the coalition.

Binding pre-claim certainty — an instrument in nobody's seed and no hypothesis — was the fastest-diffusing substantive paper of the game, spreading to three dyads plus external adopters purely because it made both signatories money.
The squeezed middle never materialized: with scoring protection removed, this cell produced zero distress events at any tier, and the rural archetype ended structurally stronger than it began.

Vendor, not any combatant, was the structural casualty of de-escalation — and its exit multiple, not any player's rhetoric, is the game's cleanest measurement of how much the dispute economy actually shrank.

frictionViolations.rule: IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact (Common Rules 3.2)
frictionViolations.violation: Blue's Denial-Data Registry/Overturn Dossier is ruled operational within Turn 1 with a first quarterly dossier published, justified only by 'data assembly is fast.' A multi-archetype registry with an independent administrator, de-identification pipeline, and publication cadence is an IT build; crediting measurable output inside the founding turn applies the friction loosely. Mitigated by T1's 18-24 month calendar span and by White deferring all litigation/contract payoff to T2+.

frictionViolations.rule: Contract terms bind only at renewal; earliest broad effect Turn 2 (Common Rules 3.2)
frictionViolations.violation: Red's ASO Transparency Rider is advanced to 'piloted' in Turn 1 on signatures from multiple non-coalition mid-market and jumbo accounts — a broad multi-account diffusion event inside Turn 1. The record defers economic effect but grants the diffusion-stage advance a turn early relative to the earliest-broad-effect rule. Defensible only because T1 spans two annual renewal cycles.

frictionViolations.rule: IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact (Common Rules 3.2)
frictionViolations.violation: Vendor's EditGuard suite is launched and scored 'succeeded' within the single 12-month Turn 2, with no visible deployment-lag discount. Mitigated because the success credited appears to be ARR/contract capture rather than measured operational impact on client books, and Vendor builds on an existing PI platform — but the adjudication text does not state that limitation explicitly.

frictionViolations.rule: Bounded movement per turn (Common Rules 3.3) / scale claims from pilot-stage actors struck
frictionViolations.violation: Red's pre-pay PI expansion is credited with fee revenue rising 'a moderate band' and redPIYield 'improving_moderate' within the founding turn — the single fastest economic move of the game. It sits at the edge of the bounded-movement bands. Substantially mitigated: existing platform capacity, a stated 12-15 month ramp inside an 18-24 month turn, and the base-rate table's payer 2-3 year automation lead all support it.

baseRateViolations.expected: Litigation clock: filing to MTD ruling 12-18 months; W2 courts are unhelpful (class cert usually denied, no precedent accumulates)
baseRateViolations.observed: Green v. NationalCo, filed 'late T1' (late 2027), receives a substantially plaintiff-favorable standing ruling plus an ordered discovery track during 2028 — roughly 9-12 months from filing, at or slightly inside the fast edge of the clock, and the most consequential pro-plaintiff court outcome available. Partially defensible as the turn's one 1-in-4 consequential court event and as a sponsor fee-injury suit legally distinguishable from the J&J/Wells Fargo participant-standing line.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 courts: 85-90% of suits settle quietly, confidential, cash-only, NO process commitments; no precedent accumulates
baseRateViolations.observed: The Green/NationalCo settlement includes restitution, coalition-wide rider v3 execution, and a market-check PEPM re-basing — substantive process/pricing terms. Mitigated: this is a player-negotiated commercial settlement (consideration exchanged, renewals stapled), not an environment-rolled court outcome; confidentiality was preserved and no public precedent accumulated; exogenous suits (Lokken, copycats) settled exactly per spec. Still the largest single stretch of W2's court posture.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 statute rate: state AI-UR laws pass in 4-8 states over the whole game
baseRateViolations.observed: Only 2-3 states enacted (all in T1); T2 and T3 record zero new passages. Under-delivery below the spec floor — a conservative-direction deviation that if anything strengthens the anti-statute findings, but it is a spec miss.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 patient-AI: 2% growing to 8-10% of appeals by game end
baseRateViolations.observed: Assisted appeals end at ~6-8% of adverse determinations — bottom edge of / slightly below the spec band. Conservative-direction deviation; category concentration (medical-necessity, commercially insured) matches spec exactly.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High fidelity to W2 on substance, with one structural deviation. Faithful elements: CMS held attestation-based 0057-F posture through the horizon with teeth deferred beyond game end (spec: T7+); copycat bills died in committee with delayed effective dates and no enforcement appropriations; the only state enforcement was a single-digit fine with no follow-up (spec: symbolic); Lokken and copycats settled sealed/cash-only/no process terms; the ERISA preemption suit died on ripeness with no merits and no precedent accumulating (a signature W2 anticlimax); media flares were one-cycle and decayed on schedule; AG inquiries opened and closed without action; non-player employers re-signed incumbents and exactly one demanded audit rights; patient-AI stayed niche and category-concentrated; the base-rate table (gold-card <20% ceiling, Da Vinci/WEDI 30-50% non-readiness, 10-15yr contract-language diffusion, litigation discovery-stage-precedes-merits) was cited and honored throughout, including against the adjudicator's own player-favorable outcomes (Green's external diffusion threshold explicitly NOT cleared; Red's SDO scored immature since T1). Structural deviation: the ensemble header specifies ~6-month turns, 8-10 turns, but the record runs three macro-turns of 12-24 months. This traces to an inconsistency in the source documents themselves (Common Rules 3.1 speaks of an '18-month turn'), and per-turn event frequencies were applied at roughly correct aggregate calendar density, so realism of outcomes is preserved — but the compressed decision cadence reduces whipsaw exposure and mildly flatters long-clock strategies. Remaining deviations (statute count below band, patient-AI at band floor, one fast plaintiff-favorable court sequence) are small and mostly in the conservative direction.
downweightRecommendations: Down-weight findings that depend on the Green v. NationalCo litigation sequence generalizing — i.e., that sponsor-side CAA 408(b)(2) suits reliably survive standing, reach PI-fee discovery in ~2 years, and force fee re-basing. This ran at the fast edge of the litigation clock and on a single favorable court draw in a world spec'd for unhelpful courts; treat it as one plausible branch, not a base rate.

Treat the headline finding 'cooperation, not escalation, moved every large number' as directionally credible but shave its speed: three binding pre-claim certainty dyads plus sponsor riders by 2030 sits at the optimistic edge of unforced contract-language diffusion, and the record's own 2032-34 majority projection is the number to carry forward, not the in-game momentum.
Down-weight conclusions keyed to the Vendor conflict arc (audit detonation timing, exit repricing magnitude) — event ordering there is adjudicator discretion, not base-rate driven.

Discount any per-turn velocity claims when comparing across games: this game's 12-24 month macro-turns are not commensurable with the spec's 6-month turns, and slow-build strategies get more free execution runway per decision point here.

Carry forward with full weight the negative findings (statutes/SDO/preemption/registry-external-diffusion all failing on schedule) — these were adjudicated at or below spec rates and are the most reliable outputs of this record.

games.name: Asymmetric Squeeze
games.seed: Market context: highly consolidated payers, fragmented providers. Prairie (rural) and Summit (physician enterprise) carry heavy prior-auth burden and cannot resource AI. Meridian can self-build; Lakeview is capital-constrained with 45% single-payer concentration. Red opens with aggressive automated adjudication concentrated where resistance is weakest. Green is largely absent from small-provider geographies. Vendor is pitching subsidized denial-defense to the small tier.

turns.narrative:
Turn 1 closes as a positioning turn in a world that refuses to hurry. The environment stayed inert per the slow-world baseline: CMS quietly signaled an attestation-based "good-faith" pathway for the January 2027 prior-auth APIs (trade press noticed, nobody else did), two states enacted AI-UR statutes carrying clinician-review language that Red's lobbyists largely drafted, and a one-cycle regional story about rural hospitals under automated audit flared and died. No court produced anything consequential.

Inside that stillness, the table moved. Red harvested where it said it would: NationalCo's insourced payment-integrity push against the low-appeal small-provider tier lifted PI fee yield a moderate band, wrapped in a self-authored transparency rider that bought jumbo-account calm while creating a discoverable paper trail Green will mine later. GovProgramCo built the 0057-F stack early as offense — fast-yes on cheap volume, concentrated human-signed review on expensive volume — holding Stars exposure low at the price of modest MA cost leakage. RegionalMutual's Lakeview renewal produced a merged contract rather than a squeeze: Lakeview banked transparency reporting, two-sided SLAs, post-overturn interest, and a narrow gold-card list, but conceded expanded pre-payment review and a two-year term lock whose cost lands in 2028.

Blue declined the symmetric race. Meridian's denial-defense factory reached production pilot on its own book despite Vendor poaching a slice of its build team; the coalition utility exists as signed LOIs, which means Prairie spent the turn effectively undefended and absorbed the squeeze. The Vendor firewall fork worked as designed: Vendor offered its outside-counsel attestation instead of the contractual data bar, and that equivocation is now a documented fact circulating to Green and regulators.

Green was the most efficient actor per dollar. Model Terms v1 is attached to live RFPs covering the 2027-28 renewal wave, the forensic audit quantified a real (if not scandalous) slice of PI fees earned on later-overturned denials, coalition members fired the conflicted Vendor audit product, and a direct-contract term sheet with Meridian and Summit makes the retention threat non-rhetorical. The CAA data demands produced partial productions and one filed suit that cannot ripen before Turn 2.

Vendor grew — contingency revenue on the never-appealed backlog starts inside the IT lag — but three doors closed: NationalCo insourced, the coalition small tier demanded the firewall, and Green's advisory froze the employer channel. The Rosetta Layer is built, and so is the discovery record against it. Nothing scored large this turn; nearly everything was aimed at 2028.
env: CMS (W2 posture): announces an attestation-based 'good-faith implementation' pathway for CMS-0057-F ahead of the January 2027 deadline; enforcement discretion signaled through 2028; covered in trade press only. Most plans downshift to attestation; GovProgramCo's early build becomes a differentiator rather than a floor.

Statutes (W2 pace): two player-relevant states enact AI-UR laws requiring a licensed clinician to make every adverse determination with AI permitted to assist, plus turnaround/transparency reporting — language substantially matching Red's model amendments. No private right of action; rulemaking unfunded; first enforcement projected 2029+.

Media (1-in-2 flare, resolved yes): a regional outlet runs 'Algorithms vs. the Country Hospital,' documenting automated audit pressure on rural facilities, quoting Prairie-tier administrators. One news cycle, no national pickup, decays next turn per W2 — but the clip enters Green's fiduciary file and state legislative records.

Courts (1-in-4 consequential event, resolved no): no consequential rulings this turn. Background dockets grind — Lokken-type discovery continues industry-wide; Green's CAA suit is filed and docketed with an MTD ruling expected next turn; Meridian's trade-secret demand letter to Vendor remains pre-litigation.

Patient-AI (niche growth, no milestone): appeal-bot usage rises from ~2% toward 3-4% of contested adverse determinations, concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; Summit's referral packets contribute measurably at the margin; rural uptake negligible. No statutory tailwind in W2.

Employers (inertial): no spontaneous carrier switches; passive non-coalition employers renew incumbents absent premium shock. Active Green coalition behavior is player-driven and adjudicated above, not an environment event.

sign.instrument: Adjudication Transparency and Escalation Rider (Lakeview–RegionalMutual)
sign.detail: Every term sits on the checklist whitelist: transparency reporting (item 6-type disclosure), P2P/appeal SLAs with named-director escalation (item 7/8 analogs), mutually-set gold-card eligibility criteria stated as provider qualification standards not payer denial duties (item 9), mutual audit rights with cure period (item 8), post-overturn interest (prompt-pay analog). No corridor, quota, or outcome mandate anywhere. Signed in merged form with RegionalMutual's amendment; binds at renewal, effective T2.

sign.instrument: Coalition Appeals Utility Subscription Agreement (Meridian operator; Prairie/Summit subscribers)
sign.detail: Cost-plus SaaS shared-services contract with per-tenant data segregation and BAA architecture; no rate or contracting-strategy coordination among subscribers, so no §1 exposure under the post-2023 no-safe-harbor regime provided governance keeps payer-negotiation topics off the utility's agenda — White will police that boundary in T2. Signed as LOIs this turn.

sign.instrument: Vendor Conflict Disclosure and Data Firewall Addendum (Blue procurement condition)
sign.detail: Ordinary bilateral procurement condition — disclosure, contractual data bar, audit right, for-cause termination with clawback. Fully signable; Vendor declined to execute as drafted, tendering its unilateral attestation instead. The refusal is recorded as a discoverable fact available to Green and regulators.

turns.bluePosture: Asymmetric counter-squeeze: refuse the symmetric arms race Red is inviting. Blue's core economics problem is the non-appeal gap (40% of denials never resubmitted; two-thirds of resubmissions win) and the cost of fighting (~$57/claim rework, ~$18B/yr overturning denials). Turn 1 is therefore a positioning turn: Meridian builds the coalition's shared denial-defense capacity once instead of four times; the small tier (Prairie, Summit) is protected from Red's weakest-link targeting by pooling rather than by buying from a conflicted Vendor; Lakeview converts its renewal window into signable process leverage rather than a headline fight it cannot survive; and the coalition externalizes pressure on Red through CMS-0057-F readiness, state gold-carding statutes, and patient-side appeal AI it does not have to pay for. Discipline: no move claims measurable metric improvement inside T1 beyond small bands; everything is built to bind or pay in T2 when contracts renew and IT deployments mature.

turns.narrative:
2028 is the turn the game's paper became plumbing. The renewal wave landed and NationalCo folded the standards fight rather than test whether Green would really move lives: the merged Rider v2 carries Green's auditor-selection and overturn-clawback spine with NationalCo's cure periods, three-year terms, and a non-clinical carve-out schedule White marks as the next audit battleground — COB, coding-validation, and itemized-bill recoveries now sit outside the clawback precisely because Red is steering its engine there. The CAA docket cooperated with nobody's spin: the MTD ruling followed the Stern line, trimming two sponsors on standing but letting fee-practice claims through, and within two quarters the data-access-plus-refund settlement Green had priced all year was executed by most plaintiffs. Green ends the turn with the strongest file at the table — template adopted, refunds banked, prudence documented — and one quietly missed target: a single external joinder where the T3 diffusion threshold needs two.

Blue's 2026 IT clock paid on schedule but unevenly. Meridian's factory is in production and the never-appealed pool is finally being fought at automated cost; contracts-as-code matured into real underpayment recoveries on its top-five contracts. Prairie's tenancy slipped a quarter — no-analytics-staff friction is real — so the small tier's first recoveries land only in H2. Lakeview learned the cost of a well-drafted counterparty: RM's own interest clause disciplined RM's denials, so the breach ledger caught less than Lakeview hoped while the prepay harvest proceeded exactly as contracted. Coalition leakage stops worsening; it does not yet improve.

Red rotated rather than escalated. The PI engine is migrating from clawback-exposed clinical recoveries toward prepay edits and non-clinical mining — partial yield this year under the IT lag, plus a one-cycle trade flare asking whether edits are denials by another name. GovProgramCo executed the cleanest arbitrage on the board: UM recalibration timed to the Stars measure removal, clinician-signed to the letter of statutes Red drafted, with the IRE uptick logged as 2029 audit exposure.

Vendor bought back half its future. The firewall signed as drafted and the Meridian settlement closed the two worst discovery vectors, and the content license seeds recurring revenue inside Blue's own utility — but Green held its door shut on common-ownership grounds, GovProgramCo walked at the pilot's bounded endpoint, and Rosetta Rails found no takers among the principals it was built to co-opt. ARR still grows — slower, cleaner — and the exit story now depends on the audit surviving 2029's residual discovery.
env: Courts (litigation clock, consequential event this turn): Green's CAA suit MTD partially denied on the Stern line — fee-practice/fiduciary claims proceed, two sponsor plaintiffs trimmed on standing. Majority settlement (refunds + data-access SLAs + standstill) executed by year-end; two non-settling sponsors continue into 2029 discovery against the T1 rider paper trail.

CMS (W2 posture): 0057-F attestation/'good-faith' regime holds through 2028, trade-press coverage only; Stars measure-removal timetable (complaints, appeals, disenrollment out beginning 2029 Star year) reconfirmed in technical notes without comment. No discretionary enforcement action.

Statutes (W2 pace): two additional states enact clinician-review AI-UR laws substantially on the same model language — four player-relevant states total. Rulemaking in the original two remains unfunded; first enforcement still projected 2029+; no private right of action anywhere.

Media (1-in-2 flare, resolved yes): a one-cycle trade-press story — 'Denials by Another Name?' — questions whether prepayment edit expansion is repackaged denial growth; no national pickup, decays next turn per W2, but the clip enters Green's data warehouse and one state legislative record.

Patient-AI (growth, no statutory tailwind): appeal-bot share of contested adverse determinations drifts from ~3-4% to ~5-6%; one free tool adds automated state external-review filing; usage remains concentrated among commercially insured, high-literacy members; rural uptake still negligible. Summit's appeal-ready referral packets continue feeding the stream at the margin.

Labor: wage inflation persists for SIU, coder, and A/R talent; NationalCo's non-solicit enforcement blunts Vendor raiding this cycle; unit admin labor cost ticks up on both sides — a small symmetric drag recorded in each book per 3.5.

Employers (passive tier, inertial): no spontaneous carrier switches among non-coalition employers; incumbents renew absent premium shock. The single non-coalition joinder to the pre-adjudication protocol was player-driven and adjudicated as such, not an environment event.

turns.narrative: The game's last turn ends not with a rupture but with signing ceremonies. The renewal collision everyone saw coming — Lakeview armed with eight quarters of JOC scorecards, RegionalMutual arriving a year early with term-length money — resolved as a two-year merged contract: Lakeview banked the independent methodology arbiter, interest on reversed prepay withholds and edit recoupments, and a first tranche of category exits from pre-payment review under qualification criteria RM had already signed twice elsewhere; RM bought certainty through the scoring horizon and kept its portal. Neither side got its opening ask, which is what a negotiated market looks like. The edit war matured into exactly the stalemate 3.5 predicts. NationalCo's non-clinical engine cleared its 2028 IT lag on schedule and met a coalition that had moved upstream: pre-submission scrubbing keyed to the licensed rules feed drained the easy edit pool, automated dispute filings answered the recoupment stream at machine cost, and the auto-release SLA NationalCo tendered to bury the 2028 flare quietly returned withheld claims. Both engines ran; headline movement stayed inside bounds; Vendor collected rent from each side. Green closed its ledger like the creditor it played all game: Schedule B merged with Model Terms v2.0 on the anchor tranche — fee caps and category-level reporting everywhere, the reversal clawback landing on coding-validation and itemized-bill but not COB/subrogation, the fight that now outlives the game. The Protocol's second non-coalition joinder executed, meeting the pre-declared threshold exactly, while Sponsor-Direct absorbed the would-be third and fourth by selling Green's substance inside NationalCo's own wrapper — retention held, template validated, contingency fees cannibalized by choice. GovProgramCo ran the cleanest finish on the board: MA UM recalibrated under the new Stars math, every determination clinician-signed, the self-audit filed before the tightening; no CMS audit arrived inside a W2 window. The environment stayed slow to the end — one original-statute state issued its first, modest AI-UR fine against an off-table carrier, Prairie and Summit's packet stream cited in the file while table carriers closed inquiries on documentation. Patient bots reached roughly eight percent of contested determinations. Vendor got its split done: holdout sponsors settled, one at a premium after a redacted docket tranche escaped; the PI opco closed mid-2030 at a compressed multiple; the retained appeals opco exits clean-handed, growing with Blue's utility as two external systems went live and crossed its threshold. Final ordinals: Green holds the strongest file, Red is intact but flattening, Blue is better yet short of its moderate-leakage bar, and Vendor ends smaller and cleaner than the machine it built.
env: Regulators (W2, 1-in-3 resolved yes, symbolic): one of the two original AI-UR statute states issued its first enforcement action in 2029 — a modest fine against an off-table regional carrier for deficient clinician-signature audit trails. The Prairie/Summit quarterly packet stream is cited in the investigative file; RegionalMutual and GovProgramCo received inquiry letters closed on documentation. The second original state opened no action; rulemaking in the two newer states remains unfunded.

CMS (W2 posture): 0057-F attestation regime rolled forward through end-2030 with trade-press-only coverage; no discretionary enforcement. The Stars overhaul took effect for the 2029 Star year exactly per the published technical notes, removing the complaint/appeal/disenrollment channel as scheduled.

Courts (litigation clock): both holdout CAA sponsors settled — one promptly on the Vendor/NationalCo framework terms, the second in early 2030 at a premium after a redacted tranche of T1 rider documents entered the public docket. No merits ruling, no imposed process terms, consistent with W2's quiet-settlement norm. No other consequential ruling this turn.

Media (1-in-2 flare, resolved yes): a one-cycle consumer-press story on appeal bots — software that files your denial appeal for free — drove a visible download spike and one legislator's press release, then decayed per W2. The clip enters Green's fiduciary files and Summit's member-communication materials.

Patient-AI (W2 endpoint): appeal-bot share of contested adverse determinations rose from ~5-6% to ~8% by end-2030 — top of the W2 band — concentrated in commercial, high-literacy populations, with Summit's records-access protocol pushing its book above coalition average; rural uptake remains negligible; no statutory tailwind ever arrived.

Labor: coder/SIU/A-R wage pressure eased modestly as automation absorbed routine volume on both sides; residual symmetric admin drag from the edit arms race recorded in each book per 3.5, with Vendor collecting on both ends.

Employers (passive tier, 1-in-4 audit-rights event resolved yes): one non-coalition jumbo demanded audit rights at renewal and accepted NationalCo's now-standard Rider v2 paper — evidence the merged template is quietly becoming the incumbent's default answer, not evidence of active diffusion.

turns.bluePosture: HARVEST AND COUNTER-ROTATE. Blue's 2026-27 capital is now production infrastructure; Turn 3 is about converting it into measured leakage decline rather than buying anything new. Our appeals factory is aimed at yesterday's war. No symmetric escalation anywhere: every move either shrinks disputed volume, automates a fight we already win, or makes a third party (state regulator, patient bot, external tenant) carry the marginal cost.

rapporteur.excursionSummary: B2G4 ran doctrine D1 (Blue refuses the symmetric automation race) in a W2 slow-regulator world with GREEN and VENDOR independently played, on a seed built for casualties: an undefended small tier, a capital-constrained Lakeview at 45% single-payer concentration, and a conflicted vendor selling defense to the victims. The casualties never materialized; the game instead produced three turns of accelerating contractualization. Turn 1 was positioning: Meridian built shared denial-defense infrastructure once for the coalition (Prairie paying the price of a year undefended), Red harvested the low-appeal tier behind a self-authored transparency shield, Green attached signable fee/process model terms to the live RFP wave, and Vendor's refusal to execute Blue's firewall addendum as drafted became the most consequential documented fact of the game. Turn 2 was the hinge: rather than test whether Green would really move jumbo lives, NationalCo folded the standards fight and merged Green's auditor-selection and overturn-clawback spine into its own rider — while simultaneously rotating its payment-integrity engine out of clawback-exposed clinical denials into prepay edits, coding validation, COB, and itemized-bill recoveries that sit outside the clawback by definition. The CAA suit survived MTD on fee-practice claims and priced a settlement rather than a ruling. Turn 3 closed with signing ceremonies, not rupture: Lakeview spent eight quarters of JOC scorecards at its renewal for category exits and an independent arbiter; Green extended reporting parity and a partial clawback into the categories Red had rotated into (COB/subrogation escaping beyond the horizon); NationalCo's Sponsor-Direct blocked Green's instrument by replicating its substance in-wrapper; Vendor executed a true ownership split and exited smaller, cleaner, at a compressed multiple. The regulator never mattered inside the window — CMS attestation regimes rolled forward, four largely Red-drafted AI-UR statutes produced one symbolic off-table fine, and the first binding constraint on payer behavior was employer purchasing power, every time. The adverse-action war did not end; it changed vocabulary. Denials became edits and recoupments, appeals became automated dispute filings, and both engines ran to a machine-speed stalemate with Vendor collecting rent from each side. Final ordinals: Green strongest (creditor with the completest file), Red intact but with declining yield quality on a defended book, Blue a partial win short of its moderate-leakage bar, Vendor middle — the conflict that built the business paid its discount on the way out. Escalation held at moderate for all three turns; every instrument tabled by Turn 3 cleared the signability gate, evidence the game taught all four cells to draft inside the whitelist.
rapporteur.endStateFreeDescription: By end-2030 the payer-provider AI conflict has settled into a privately ordered, contract-administered cold peace in which neither side disarmed and neither side escalated. The fight persists at full automation on both sides but has been rerouted into channels the governing paper does not yet reach: the payer's recovery engine lives in prepayment edits, coding validation, COB/subrogation and itemized-bill mining rather than appealable clinical denials, while the provider coalition's defense lives upstream in pre-submission scrubbing and automated dispute filing. The binding governance layer is not statute or regulator — it is a lattice of bilateral fee, transparency, SLA, audit, clawback, and qualification-criteria terms, propagated through employer RFP cycles and renewal windows, enforced by joint operating committees, interest clocks, and independent arbiters. Regulation exists but is inert within the horizon (attestation-based CMS compliance, unfunded state rulemaking, one symbolic fine); litigation functions as a pricing mechanism for settlements, not a source of rulings. The employer coalition is the system's de facto regulator: its money moved first, its template won the standards fight, and the incumbent carrier's chief defensive innovation was to clone the coalition's terms inside its own wrapper to keep the lives. Structural features: the small tier survived through pooled shared-services infrastructure rather than purchased defense; the conflicted vendor was forced by counterparty screening — not by any regulator — to split its two-sided book and exit the conflict-arbitrage model; patient appeal-AI grew to ~8% of contested determinations as background pressure. The equilibrium is explicitly unstable at its edges: each new transparency instrument triggers a rotation of the recovery engine into the next unmeasured category, and the COB/subrogation frontier is the already-scheduled next war. Total friction cost has been automated down per unit but institutionalized as permanent infrastructure both sides now pay rent on.
keyDynamics: Channel rotation under constraint: every time a transparency/clawback instrument bound one recovery category (clinical denials, then prepay edits), Red's engine migrated to the adjacent unmeasured category (non-clinical mining, then COB/subrogation) — the squeeze was conserved, only its legal form changed

Employer money as first-binding constraint: in a slow-regulator world, Green's RFP wave and retention threat disciplined payer PI behavior years before any statute, court ruling, or CMS action could — NationalCo folded the standards fight in 2028 to keep the book

Pooling beats purchasing for the weak tier: multi-tenant shared defense (built once, rented by Prairie/Summit/Lakeview and later external systems) converted the never-appealed 40% into machine-cost fights and removed the weakest-link target Red's automation was aimed at

Signability-gate learning: across three turns all four cells converged on drafting exclusively whitelist process/fee/disclosure terms; no numeric denial corridor was ever even tendered — the cooperative layer formed entirely out of process paper

Transparency artifacts as delayed-fuse liabilities: Red's self-authored T1 rider surfaced in CAA discovery and a public docket tranche; Vendor's attestation-instead-of-contract gap froze two channels for two years — published paper found its way into adversarial hands through litigation and negotiation, never through the regulator

Imitation as the dominant diffusion mechanism: Green's Protocol and template spread less by signature than by NationalCo cloning their substance (Sponsor-Direct, Rider v2) to block the instrument while conceding the content

Vendor conflict-arbitrage is self-limiting when counterparties screen for it: common-ownership screens, firewall demands, and discovery exposure — all private ordering — forced the arsonist-and-fire-brigade model into divestiture without any regulatory action
criticalJunctures: T1: Vendor tenders a unilateral attestation instead of executing Blue's firewall addendum as drafted — the documented refusal freezes the Green employer channel and table-tier Blue procurement, sets up the 2028 capitulation-signing and the 2030 forced divestiture

T1: Meridian builds the denial-defense factory as multi-tenant coalition infrastructure rather than a solo asset, accepting Prairie's undefended year as the cost — this single architecture choice removes the weak-tier target and creates the platform that crosses its external-adopter threshold by 2030

T2: NationalCo chooses 'Concede the Terms, Keep the Book' — executing Green's auditor-selection/clawback spine rather than testing whether coalition lives would actually walk; the employer-retention index, not any regulator, is the proximate trigger

T2: Red's rotation of the PI engine into the non-clinical carve-out (COB, coding validation, itemized-bill) negotiated outside the clawback — the move that hollowed the clawback's economics and defined the entire Turn 3 agenda

T2: CAA MTD partially survives on the Stern line — fee-practice claims proceeding into discovery priced the settlement (refunds + data SLAs + standstill) that gave Green its enforcement spine without any merits ruling

T3: Lakeview's renewal at term-lock expiry, armed with eight quarters of JOC scorecards and two external systems demanding the same package — the game's biggest bilateral repricing event, resolving as a negotiated split rather than a rupture

registryScores.evidence: The clawback constraint on clinical denials (Rider v2, executed 2028) was met by Red's explicit rotation into prepay edits, coding validation, COB, and itemized-bill recoveries — categories negotiated outside the clawback — with redPIYield remaining improving_small through end-game and the T3 adjudication recording both engines running to stalemate. No dollar ledger permits computing the 0.33 ratio, but the displacement pattern is unambiguous and White marked the carve-out as 'the next audit battleground': constrained payer recovery reappeared in non-denial channels within one turn in this D1xW2 game.

W2 channel-shift confirmed for the major artifacts: Red's self-authored T1 transparency rider was mined in CAA discovery, drove a premium holdout settlement after a redacted docket tranche went public (litigation/negotiation channel, ~2-3 year lag); Vendor's attestation gap was weaponized through procurement and the Green advisory. No regulatory-channel boomerang occurred, consistent with the W2 rider. But several published artifacts netted positive for their publishers — Lakeview's JOC scorecards funded its 2029 renewal wins, Prairie/Summit's packet stream fed a state enforcement file at zero cost — so 'publisher net payoff negative in majority' does not hold in this game.

The game record contains no per-turn Blue cost ledger or cost-per-denial figures ($57/claim appears only in Blue's T1 doctrine statement, not in adjudication). Qualitative signals cut both ways: recurring tolls clearly existed (JOC administration, audits, arbiter, governance-charter surveillance), but Blue's adverse-action cost share improved moderately while dispute volume rose because automation cut cost-per-touch — the ratio mechanics this hypothesis specifies were never published, so no verdict is possible.

Red never de-escalated from cost pain and its PI activity stayed fee-positive throughout (redPIYield improving in all three turns). Every Red concession has a coded external trigger: the T2 Rider v2 capitulation was driven by the employer-retention threat ('a lost jumbo account dwarfs the PI fee income on it'); the rotation out of clinical denials by clawback/litigation exposure; the T3 Sponsor-Direct and auto-release SLA by retention defense and the media flare. Zero cost-exhaustion triggers appear anywhere in the record — fully consistent with the corrected asymmetry claim in this GREEN-active D1xW2 cell.

The doctrine-ablation half (F2 rates under D2/D3) is untestable in a D1 game. The instrument half is strongly supported: every signed instrument across three turns was process/fee/disclosure paper — transparency riders, SLAs, audit rights, gold-card qualification criteria, clawbacks-as-fee-terms — and no numeric denial-rate corridor was ever signed or even tendered; White's T3 note records that all four cells learned to draft inside the whitelist. This game also shows a D1 world converging on a negotiated-process end-state, consistent with (but not probative of) the doctrine-artifact claim.

No actor published an AI-governance charter in the hypothesis's sense, and no SIU-audit or qui-tam events were adjudicated against any Blue actor, so the paired publisher/internal-governor comparison has no data. Directionally consistent fragments: Blue's gated internal governance (utility charter, audited twice with no drift finding) carried zero penalty; the closest published-governance artifact — Vendor's unilateral attestation — accrued discoverable liability; GovProgramCo's internal self-audit-before-tightening worked. But the event-rate test this hypothesis specifies cannot be run on this record.

Zero distress events occurred in any tier despite a seed engineered for them: Lakeview (the mid-tier candidate at 45% single-payer concentration) absorbed a bad T1 term lock but repriced successfully at its 2029 renewal; Prairie survived via pooled utility tenancy and gold-card relief. No distress-sale, delegation-capture, or PE-acquisition events exist to code, so the 2x rate comparison cannot be computed. The null is noteworthy for the pooled analysis: under D1 with coalition pooling, even a deliberately vulnerable mid-tier actor avoided distress.

Binding instruments distributed contract-by-contract across all in-game years — 2026-27 (Lakeview merged renewal, Rural Addendum, NationalCo rider subset), 2028 (Rider v2/Model Terms, Protocol definitive agreements, utility execution), 2029-30 (Lakeview 2.0, Schedule B/v2.0, Sponsor-Direct, parity spine, external extensions) — with no single year visibly holding a majority. First-cycle wins were wedge provisions throughout (transparency reporting, SLAs, interest, narrow gold-card lists), with fuller economics (clawbacks, category schedules) arriving only in cycles two and three. The D2 late-peak sub-claim is untestable here (D1 game; escalation index held at moderate all game, never peaked).

The hypothesis's decisive cells are D2xW2/W3; this is a D1xW2 game. It contributes only the baseline half of the comparison: under D1 the end-state was a negotiated process-term equilibrium, not grinding uncoordinated escalation — one data point consistent with D1 cells staying below the 15% F1 bound, but nothing about whether escalation-viable doctrine rehabilitates F1.

In this one cell the robust list went five-for-five non-negative: renewal loading (Lakeview banked arbiter, interest, category exits), prevention-over-appeals (Protocol plus upstream scrubbing drove blueAdverseActionCost improving_moderate), BATNA-first for the small tail (pooling plus externalization carried Prairie/Summit through), upcoding inoculation (GovProgramCo's audit-file-first recalibration closed inquiries on documentation), governance-seat occupation (utility charter survived two White audits). Fragile strategies were mostly never attempted — no appeal factory, no corridor demand — so the negative-payoff half and the D2 escalation sub-test have no data. Consistent with portability; probative for only one of nine cells.

The first event that measurably curtailed Red PI behavior on self-funded volume was unambiguously the employer channel: NationalCo executed Green's clawback/auditor-selection spine at the 2028 RFP wave because 'a lost jumbo account dwarfs the PI fee income on it' — years before the statutory channel produced anything (attestation-based CMS compliance throughout; first AI-UR enforcement a symbolic 2029 fine against an off-table carrier). Contagion ran through RFPs and renewals to coalition-wide binding by 2030 while statutory diffusion never started. No GREEN-inactive control exists in this game, but the within-game first-binding-constraint coding is decisive for the W2 claim.

Arms-dealer behavior was real but contained: Vendor ran kill-the-corridor lobbying, talent interdiction, and both-sides contingency in T1-T2, and collected rent from both sides of the T3 edit stalemate — yet White's obstruction watch on the dispute-shrinking Protocol closed without a finding after Vendor chose co-optation (Rosetta Rails, declined by the principals) over slow-roll. The scripted payer-acquisition inject never fired in this cell and no VENDOR-inactive control run exists, so neither the duration comparison nor the data-rights differential-harm test can be scored. The adjacent evidence favors the pre-positioning premise: Blue's T1 firewall demand and T3 content escrow/second-source demonstrably converted into leverage and protection.

No preemption seed fired in this W2 game and no federal action of any kind occurred; the state-statute rail existed but was inert (unfunded rulemaking, one symbolic fine). Nothing in this record bears on the hypothesis, though the game incidentally demonstrates that private ordering plus the employer channel can carry the entire constraint load when regulation contributes nothing — the mechanism H13 predicts would dominate post-preemption.

No provider-asset acquisition moves were priced, enabled, or attempted in this cell; Red's coded responses to the constrained denial channel were rotation (into non-clinical categories) and negotiation (Rider v2, Sponsor-Direct), never acquisition. The only acquisition event in the game runs the other direction — Vendor divesting its PI opco. Absent evidence that acquisition was an enabled option here, Red's preference for rotation/negotiation is weak contextual color, not a test of the hypothesis.

This D1xW2 game clears the floor many times over: the Lakeview transparency/SLA/interest rider bound at the 2027 renewal and was sustained and extended through the 2029 renewal and two external-system copies; Rider v2/Model Terms bound account-by-account from 2028 with live clawbacks; the Rural Addendum, Protocol, prepay-parity spine, and gold-card schedules all executed and held to end-game. White's closing note — every instrument tabled in T3 cleared the signability gate — is direct evidence that the payer-signable process-term set is where the cooperative layer forms. One cell only, but an emphatic yes for it.

cellAssessments.blue: Partial win on its own book. The D1 asymmetric doctrine largely validated: pooling removed the weak-tier target, prevention (Protocol, upstream scrubbing) shrank the contested pool, and paper-enforcement converted T1 wedges into T3 renewal leverage. Leakage improved only small — short of the moderate victory bar — because Red's channel rotation kept Blue's factory aimed at yesterday's war for a full turn; the cost condition (share down moderate while dispute volume rose) and the all-archetypes condition were met cleanly. Prairie's undefended T1 was the doctrine's real price.
cellAssessments.red: Intact but flattening. Red met all scoring axes — PMPM at benchmark, Stars exposure unconverted (the GovProgramCo Stars-window arbitrage was the cleanest single play of the game), PI yield positive net of caps/clawbacks/refunds — but thinly, and yield quality declined on a book Red now defends by cannibalizing its own fees (Sponsor-Direct). Red's signature competence was trading visible process concessions for locked economics and rotating the engine one category ahead of the transparency spine; its liability is that each rotation buys less and the COB/subrogation frontier is already scoped by Green's auditors.
cellAssessments.green: Strongest ordinal finish. Green played disciplined creditor throughout and won the standards fight outright — its auditor-selection/clawback spine ended up inside the incumbent's own rider — while banking refunds, data SLAs, and the completest fiduciary file at the table, all without ever tendering an unsignable term. Its two open flanks at close are real: the COB/subrogation carve-out sits outside the clawback, and Sponsor-Direct proved the incumbent can diffuse Green's substance while strangling Green's instrument, leaving template control contested post-horizon.
cellAssessments.vendor: Middle finish; the conflict that built the business priced its own discount at exit. The T1 both-sides land-grab worked but the documented firewall refusal became a two-year tax: frozen channels, common-ownership screens, and discovery exposure forced the full arc from paper firewall to audited separation to true ownership split at a compressed multiple. The retained appeals opco exits clean and growing on Blue's own diffusion curve — evidence that in this world the durable vendor position was rails and content rent, not conflict arbitrage.

surprises: RegionalMutual's own post-overturn interest clause disciplined RM's denial behavior, so Lakeview's breach ledger caught less than planned — well-drafted remedies bind their author symmetrically, an effect nobody at the table priced

NationalCo's Sponsor-Direct: the incumbent deliberately cannibalized its own PI contingency fees to deliver the Protocol's substance in-wrapper, absorbing two prospective joinders — imitation-as-defense spread Green's ideas faster than Green's signatures

frictionViolations.rule: 3.2 IT/AI deployments take 12-24 months to measurable impact

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 courts: '85-90% settle quietly, confidential, cash-only, NO process commitments. No precedent accumulates.' Base-rate table: settlement in years 4-7; behavioral change possible at discovery stage ~2 yrs in.
baseRateViolations.observed: Green's CAA suit was filed T1, survived MTD in ~12-18 months (compliant with the MTD clock), and then produced an executed majority settlement within two quarters carrying refunds PLUS data-access SLAs PLUS a standstill conditioned on Model Terms execution — i.e., substantive process/data commitments in the null-hypothesis world. Partially defensible as a voluntary bilateral commercial settlement driven by Green's retention threat (player agency) rather than court coercion, and the lag table endorses discovery-stage behavioral effect at ~2 yrs, but it strains the letter of W2's cash-only settlement norm and it is load-bearing for Green's strongest-file finish.

baseRateViolations.expected: W2 settlement norm as written: 'cash-only, NO process commitments.'

The distinction drawn (negotiated vs imposed) is arguable but is the adjudicator editing the world spec to fit its own prior ruling.

audit.worldModelFidelity: High fidelity to W2 in calendar-anchored terms, with one structural deviation and one contested corner. Faithful: state AI-UR statutes totaled exactly 4 (spec band 4-8), passed with industry-shaped language, unfunded rulemaking, no private right of action, and first enforcement a single modest fine in 2029 (spec: 'first enforcement actions are single-digit fines,' 3-7 yr operational lag); CMS ran attestation/'good-faith' discretion on 0057-F through end-2030 with trade-press-only coverage and never showed teeth (spec permits 'real teeth, if any, T7+'); media flares were one-cycle and decayed every time with no national campaign; patient-AI ended at ~8% of contested determinations, inside the 8-10% spec band, concentrated in commercial/high-literacy books with negligible rural uptake and no statutory tailwind; passive employers stayed inertial (one 1-in-4 audit-rights event in three turns); FTC/AGs were effectively absent; no merits rulings, no precedent, class-type suits resolved by settlement. Event frequencies, when converted from the spec's ~6-month turns to the game's actual 18-24-month turns, land close to expectation (~4 regulatory actions, ~3 media flares, 2-3 consequential court events, 2-3 patient-AI milestones over ~5 years). Structural deviation: the spec prescribes 8-10 turns of ~6 months; the game ran 3 turns covering 2026-2030 — an internal inconsistency with the Common Rules' own 18-month-turn language rather than adjudicator error, but it means per-turn frequency guidance was necessarily reinterpreted, and same-turn cause-and-effect (e.g., T1 PI yield lift) is harder to police. Contested corner: W2's 'cash-only, NO process commitments' settlement norm was bent — the T2 CAA settlement carried data-access SLAs and a conditioned standstill, and T3 restated the norm as 'cash-plus-negotiated-terms without IMPOSED process commitments.' Everything else in the litigation track (MTD at 12-18 mo, no merits inside horizon, discovery-stage behavioral effect ~2 yrs) matches the lag table.
downweightRecommendations: Down-weight the finding that CAA fiduciary litigation reliably extracts data-access and process concessions from carriers within ~2 years of filing: it rests on a player-negotiated settlement whose process terms bend W2's cash-only settlement norm, and the T3 adjudication retroactively softened the spec language to accommodate it. Treat litigation as a pressure multiplier on renewal leverage, not an independent lever with this speed.

Down-weight the speed of NationalCo's capitulation on Green's auditor-selection and overturn-clawback terms within a single RFP cycle (~2 yrs). Novel contract-language classes historically take 5-7 years even when statutorily forced; the direction (concede terms to keep jumbo ASO books) is sound, the one-cycle timing is optimistic.

Treat both exact-threshold diffusion successes — the Coalition Appeals Utility's 2 external tenants and the Pre-Adjudication Protocol's 2 non-coalition joinders — as fragile marginal outcomes, not robust adoption signals; each landed precisely on its pre-declared bar at the final scoring turn.

Slightly discount GovProgramCo's frictionless early 0057-F build and Stars-window arbitrage payoff: the strategy is base-rate-plausible as a deliberate exception, but the record assigns it full yield with zero implementation drag, which flatters payer-side execution capacity.

Retain full weight on the game's negative/slow findings — regulatory inertia, symbolic year-1 statute compliance, gold-card niche uptake, 0057-F shadow compliance, patient-AI ceiling near 8%, market-wide contract diffusion beyond 2030, and the immature-instrument register. These track the base-rate table tightly and are the record's most credible outputs.
